title: Thrombectomy provides 1-year gains for patients with severe stroke
content:
A one-year follow-up analysis of a landmark clinical trial suggests that patients with severe strokes experienced better long-term outcomes after undergoing endovascular thrombectomy compared with medical management alone, according to findings published in JAMA.
The study evaluated ischemic stroke patients presenting with large-core infarcts, meaning a significant amount of brain tissue had suffered damage. These patients are historically considered less likely to benefit from mechanical clot removal because of the amount of brain damage that has already occurred by the time treatment begins, said Sameer A. Ansari, MD, Ph.D., professor and chief of Interventional Neuroradiology in the Department of Radiology, who was a co-author of the study.
While the original trial did not show meaningful benefit at 90 days, the newly reported one-year data show functional gains among patients who received thrombectomy. The results of the current study suggest longer-term follow-up was needed to fully understand the benefits of the procedure, Ansari said.
"At one year, it's quite evident based on the statistical analysis that there's significant benefit with thrombectomy," said Ansari, also a professor in the Ken and Ruth Davee Department of Neurology and of Neurological Surgery.
One-year gains come into focus
In the study, investigators found that 23.6% of patients treated with endovascular thrombectomy achieved functional independence one year after their stroke, compared with 6.8% of patients who received medical management. Patients in the thrombectomy group were also significantly more likely to regain the ability to walk independently, with 35.4% achieving independent walking versus 18% in the medical-management group.
The multicenter trial enrolled patients at 47 U.S. stroke centers who presented within 24 hours of symptom onset and had large strokes identified using noncontrast computed tomography (CT) imaging.
Patients who underwent thrombectomy also reported better quality of life one year after stroke, while one-year mortality rates were similar between the treatment groups.
The findings add to growing evidence from other large-core interventional stroke trials that patients with extensive brain injury can still benefit from rapid thrombectomy to restore blood flow.
Recovery may extend beyond 90 days
One possible explanation for the delayed benefit, Ansari said, is that recovery from severe stroke continues long after the standard 90-day assessment period used in most clinical trials.
"We know that people continue to improve after a stroke for the next one to two years," Ansari said. "Three months has been an arbitrary standard used in prior stroke trials to assess benefit and functional outcomes after targeted interventions."
Restoring blood flow may also support long-term neuroplasticity, the brain's ability to reorganize and form new neural connections after injury, Ansari said. The study reported that patients who received thrombectomy continued to improve between 90 days and one year, while outcomes remained static or declined in the medical-management group.
While more research is needed to fully understand which large-core stroke patients benefit most from thrombectomy, the results of the study may provide additional confidence that aggressive intervention can yield meaningful recovery for patients, even when improvement is not immediately apparent.
"What we're seeing across multiple randomized controlled trials, endovascular thrombectomy remains a powerful intervention across a spectrum of stroke presentations," Ansari said. "It gives clinicians more confidence to treat patients even with severe brain injury and to counsel their loved ones that the outcome benefit may require time to heal, hard work with physical therapy/rehabilitation, and family support."

title: ウクライナから避難の母親、大阪に交流拠点「文化を守り、伝えたい」
content:
ウクライナから避難の母親、大阪に交流拠点「文化を守り、伝えたい」
ロシアによる全面侵攻から24日で4年半。ウクライナから子どもを連れて日本に避難した母親2人が23日、ウクライナ文化の発信と交流の拠点を開設した。大阪市内の廃校を活用した施設の一室に、「小さなウクライナ」が生まれた。
ロシアの全面侵攻が始まった2022年、オリシャ・ギルナさん（40）は長男（15）を、ナタリヤ・デレビヤンコさん（48）は長女（16）と次女（9）を連れて日本に避難した。大阪市の市営住宅で暮らしている。
2人は24年、他の避難民とともに一般社団法人「ドドム」を立ち上げた。チャリティーイベントを開いてウクライナ文化を発信し、ウクライナの人たちに義援金を送るなどしてきた。
だが、ドドムに活動の拠点はなかった。
出入国在留管理庁によると、7月末時点でウクライナ避難民1935人が日本で暮らす。ウクライナ料理店や語学教室は東京などにある。だがそれでも、日本でウクライナ文化に触れられる場は限られている。
子どもたちがウクライナ語で遊べて、ウクライナの文化を日本の人たちにも知ってもらえる拠点をつくりたい――。
2人は1年ほど前から場所を探してきた。
ドドムはボランティアで運営していて、予算は限られる。さまざまな役所に相談し、日本人に名刺を渡すたびに適した場がないか尋ねた。
そうするなかで、友人からこの場所を紹介された。
廃校になった元小学校を活用した大阪市生野区の多文化交流施設「いくのパーク」。旧校舎3階の教室だった一室に色鮮やかな刺繡（ししゅう）を施した民族衣装やウクライナ語の絵本が並べられ、23日、「ウクライナ文化交流センター ドドム」がオープンした。
開設式典では、参加者約100人がウクライナ国歌を斉唱したほか、民族衣装を着たウクライナの子どもたちが踊りを披露した。
「ウクライナは戦争のイメージが付いてしまったが、おいしい料理も、楽しい祭りも、美しい伝統もある。そのことを知ってほしい」とオリシャさん。
ウクライナ避難民の生活を支援してきたという日本人男性（55）は「日本ではウクライナへの関心や支援がだんだん下火になっていると感じていた。ここで交流を育むことで、もっと活発化してほしい」と話す。
センターではこれから、ウクライナに関する展示会やウクライナ語を学べる教室、ペトリキウカ（ウクライナの伝統的な絵）を描けるワークショップなどを定期的に催す予定だ。
センター開設の背景には、今も戦争が続いている現実がある。
ナタリヤさんの夫はキーウ近郊の街で暮らす。長男（24）は兵士として戦場にいる。
発電所も爆撃された。祖父母…

title: Tenn. S. Ct. Lets Stand Decision That Copyright Law Doesn't Bar Release of Covenant Shooter Manifesto
content:
The Volokh Conspiracy
Mostly law professors | Sometimes contrarian | Often libertarian | Always independent
Tenn. S. Ct. Lets Stand Decision That Copyright Law Doesn't Bar Release of Covenant Shooter Manifesto
Last week, the Tennessee Supreme Court denied the parents' application to review the Tennessee Court of Appeals' ruling, so that now goes into effect. Here's my post on the Court of Appeals ruling, from February:
[* * *]
Following the 2023 Covenant School shooting in Nashville, in which the shooter was killed by responding police officers, the shooter's parents inherited the shooter's copyright interest in various writings (including the shooter's manifesto). They then assigned it "to a trust to be held for the benefit of the Covenant Parents' children," and the Covenant Parents argued that this should keep the writings from being released. The trial court agreed, but yesterday's Tennessee Court of Appeals opinion in Brewer v. Metro. Gov't of Nashville (Judge Kristi Davis, joined by Judges John McClarty and Thomas Frierson) basically rejected the copyright argument for nondisclosure:
The trial court and the Parents … conflate the concept of access for inspection [which wouldn't itself implicate the Copyright Act -EV] with reproduction and display [which might potentially implicate the Act, subject to the fair use defense -EV]. Indeed, the TPRA requires that "[a]ll state, county and municipal records shall, at all times during business hours, which for public hospitals shall be during the business hours of their administrative offices, be open for personal inspection by any citizen of this state …"
We interpret the TPRA broadly to promote access to the records, in keeping with the statutory purpose. Considering this statutory purpose, we can construe the TPRA in such a way that does not require Metro to publicly display its file. Nor need Metro distribute the records to the public; rather, Metro need only allow Petitioners access for personal inspection. Although the Act protects the means by which copyrighted material may be obtained, the Act itself does not inure total confidentiality and secrecy.
As another state court confronted with this issue noted, "[o]ne could certainly disclose a record without either reproducing or distributing the same record." Nat'l Council on Tchr. Quality v. Curators of Univ. of Mo. (Mo. Ct. App. 2014); see also Ali v. Phila. City Plan. Comm'n (Pa. Commw. Ct. 2015) ("[N]ot every disclosure of copyrighted material without the owner's consent violates the Copyright Act."). By the same token, Metro may allow access to the records for personal inspection without itself copying, displaying, or publishing the records. This result "allow[s] the public to scrutinize [Metro's] reliance on or consideration of the copyrighted material[,]" thus furthering the purposes of the TPRA.
That said, we acknowledge the potential issue foreseen by the trial court. Assuming for argument that the Parents hold a valid copyright and that Petitioners seek copies of the material pursuant to section 10-7-506, where does this leave Metro as the records custodian? In Ali, the Pennsylvania appellate court explained this dilemma well:
Although the rights conferred on the copyright holder are subject to "fair use," the Copyright Act is nonetheless problematic for local agencies when faced with a RTKL [Right-To-Know Law] request that seeks copyrighted materials. Unless the copyright holder has consented to duplication, duplication of the copyrighted material under the RTKL carries the risk that the copyright holder will sue the local agency for infringement in federal court.
If found to be an infringer, the local agency could be held liable to the copyright holder for actual or statutory damages, which, in the case of willful infringement, could be up to $150,000. The local agency could also be ordered to pay the copyright owner's costs and attorneys' fees. All the while, the local agency is expending taxpayer dollars in costs and attorneys' fees to defend itself in an infringement action occasioned not by its own assessment of the risk and subsequent voluntary disclosure, but by forced disclosure by [court order].
This concern, while reasonable, falls outside the scope of what we must decide today. This is a TPRA case in which Metro is the respondent. Thus, our ruling is narrowly tailored to address only Metro's obligations under the TPRA and whether it can meet that obligation without running afoul of the Act. Construing the TPRA broadly to promote access to public records, as we are required, we conclude that under these particular circumstances, the only overt action Metro must take to meet its obligation is to allow Petitioners access to the records for personal inspection. Although we acknowledge the copying rights conferred to the public by section 10-7-506, we do not opine whether it is advisable for Petitioners to copy or otherwise reproduce those records upon said personal inspection and access.
Simply put, so long as Metro maintains the records, it must allow Petitioners access to same for personal inspection. Whether Petitioners choose to go further than that considering their potential copyright liability is left to them. Likewise, if the Parents wish to pursue a copyright infringement action against Petitioners based on how the Petitioners choose to use the information in the records, the Act provides the Parents with that remedy. See Nat'l Council on Tchr. Quality v. Minn. State Colls. & Univs. (Minn. Ct. App. 2013) ("If [Minnesota law] requires a Minnesota governmental entity, such as MnSCU, to release copies of public data, the person or entity receiving the data takes the information subject to the owner's [federal copyright] rights. All of the author's rights and remedies under the [Act] are unimpeded.").
The Parents argue that the weight of authority on this issue supports their position. Respectfully, our research suggests otherwise. The cases addressing the issue before us reflect a variety of results. For example, several courts have held that while the Act applies to public records, the fair use limitation, found at 17 U.S.C. section 107, allows the records to be copied. See, e.g., Zellner v. Cedarburg Sch. Dist. (Wisc. 2007) ("Applying the 'fair use' factors outlined in 17 U.S.C. § 107 in this case, we are satisfied that the CD and the memo do not fall within the copyright exception under Wis. Stat. § 19.32(2)."); Nat'l Council on Tchr. Quality (fair use allowed disclosure under Minnesota law where requestor, a non-profit working for educational reform, planned to use the information for "criticism, comment, … scholarship, or research"); ACLU of Utah Found., Inc. v. Davis Cnty. (Utah Dist. Ct. 2021) (concluding "that the laws of copyright do not limit the release of the Utah Jail Standards to these Petitioners for the uses they have outlined[,]" where "the type of use envisioned by these Petitioners falls easily within the fair use doctrine of federal copyright law"); State ex rel. Rea v. Ohio Dep't of Educ. (Ohio 1998) ("Exceptions to public records requests do not include the copyright defense where the public records fall under the 'fair-use' exception to the federal copyright statute or where the copyrighted material is purchased by the public office or agency that is the subject of the public records request."). {Petitioners argue on appeal that the fair use exception allows Metro to release the disputed records. In light of our decision that the TPRA and Act do not conflict here, we need not delve into Petitioners' intended uses for the information.}
On the other hand, at least one court has rejected the fair use argument, finding that to be the sole purview of the federal courts. Curators of Univ. of Mo. ("[T]his court lacks the authority to determine whether a particular use of copyrighted materials constitutes fair use, as federal courts have 'original jurisdiction of any civil action arising under the [Act].'"); see also Pictometry Int'l Corp. v. Freedom of Info. Comm'n (Conn. 2013) (noting that the court lacks "jurisdiction to determine whether a particular use of copyrighted materials infringes on the copyright holder's rights under federal copyright law or, instead, constitutes a fair use of the materials").
Accordingly, there is no weight of authority as the Parents suggest. Rather, the results vary and depend in part upon the language of the state law at issue. And here, the TPRA's text provides a solution that allows Metro to comply with Petitioners' requests while avoiding conflict with the Act…. Metro can satisfy its obligations under the TPRA by allowing Petitioners to access the records for personal inspection, thereby avoiding conflict with the Act. To the extent Petitioners then engage in actionable conduct under the Act, the Parents may pursue the remedy available to them, as those remedies remain unimpeded, and Petitioners can raise any relevant defenses….
Note that I was one of the many signers of an amicus brief (UPDATE: full PDF) arguing against using copyright law to limit disclosure of the writings; many thanks to Vanderbilt's Stanton Foundation First Amendment Clinic (Jennifer Safstrom) and Intellectual Property & the Arts Clinic (Michael B. Bressman) for representing us on that brief, and to Clinical Legal Fellow Ryan Riedmueller, who helped with the brief.

title: Un estudio reivindica la aportación de los científicos con discapacidad: "Aportan perspectivas únicas"
content:
Un estudio reivindica la aportación de los científicos con discapacidad: "Aportan perspectivas únicas"
Basado en hechos observados y verificados directamente por nuestros periodistas o por fuentes informadas.
Elígenos como tu fuente preferida en Google.
Según un estudio publicado en la revista 'Research in Science Education', los científicos con discapacidad "desarrollan formas especialmente creativas de hacer ciencia".
Los científicos con discapacidad reclaman ser vistos como productores de conocimiento complementario y novedoso y no únicamente como beneficiarios de políticas de inclusión, según un estudio recién publicado en la revista científica 'Research in Science Education', que sostiene que la experiencia de la discapacidad puede enriquecer la práctica investigadora y aportar nuevas perspectivas a la generación de conocimiento científico.
La investigación, titulada '(dis)Ability in Science: How Scientists with Disabilities Embody the Nature of Science as a Human Endeavor', fue realizada por Mila Rosa Librea-Carden y Jonathan L. Hall, de la University of Central Florida, y por Sarah H. Losoya, de la University of Northern Colorado, ambas de Estados Unidos. El estudio analiza cómo los investigadores con discapacidad entienden y representan la denominada "naturaleza de la ciencia", un concepto que hace referencia a la forma en que se construye el conocimiento científico y al papel que desempeñan en ese proceso factores humanos, sociales y culturales.
Los autores subrayaron que, pese al creciente interés por la diversidad en el ámbito académico, las experiencias de los científicos con discapacidad han permanecido "largamente inexploradas" en la literatura científica, especialmente en relación con la forma en que esa experiencia influye en el desarrollo de la actividad investigadora.
El trabajo plantea que la discapacidad "no debe considerarse únicamente desde una perspectiva de barreras o limitaciones", sino también como una "fuente de experiencias que puede aportar enfoques novedosos a la investigación". En este sentido, sostiene que "quienes desarrollan su carrera científica conviviendo con una discapacidad pueden identificar problemas, necesidades y preguntas de investigación que pasan desapercibidos para otros investigadores".
Las conclusiones se extrajeron de una investigación cualitativa que incluyó 21 entrevistas en profundidad a siete científicos de reconocido prestigio que se identificaron como personas con discapacidad. Los participantes pertenecían a disciplinas tan diversas como la oceanografía, la genética, la ecología, la microbiología y la neurociencia.
Los autores señalan que las experiencias de los científicos con discapacidad "han sido tradicionalmente ignoradas en los estudios sobre la naturaleza de la ciencia". Su objetivo fue analizar cómo estas experiencias "influyen en la forma de investigar y producir conocimiento científico. Una de las principales conclusiones es que los científicos con discapacidad "desarrollan formas especialmente creativas de hacer ciencia".
Los autores señalan que las experiencias de los científicos con discapacidad "han sido tradicionalmente ignoradas en los estudios sobre la naturaleza de la ciencia"
Más allá de la incusión
Según los investigadores, la presencia de personas con discapacidad en los laboratorios, universidades y centros de investigación "no solo representa una cuestión de igualdad de oportunidades, sino también una oportunidad para mejorar la calidad y la relevancia social de la ciencia".
El estudio defiende que las vivencias asociadas a la discapacidad "contribuyen al desarrollo de competencias relacionadas con la adaptación, la creatividad, la resolución de problemas y la identificación de barreras", capacidades que pueden repercutir positivamente en la práctica científica.
Asimismo, concluye que las personas con discapacidad aportan "perspectivas que siguen estando poco representadas en la comunidad investigadora" y que reconocer estas contribuciones intelectuales resulta tan importante como garantizar el acceso de las personas con discapacidad a las carreras científicas.
Ciencia más humana
Uno de los principales hallazgos que expone el artículo es que "la experiencia de la discapacidad refuerza la idea de que la ciencia es una actividad profundamente humana y condicionada por las trayectorias personales de quienes la desarrollan".
A juicio de los autores, los científicos con discapacidad "ayudan a visibilizar cómo factores como la experiencia vital, el contexto social o las barreras del entorno influyen en la producción de conocimiento", cuestionando la imagen de una ciencia completamente desvinculada de las circunstancias de las personas que la practican.
Entre las principales conclusiones de la investigación destacan que los científicos con discapacidad "aportan perspectivas únicas para comprender la naturaleza de la ciencia"; que la discapacidad "puede enriquecer los procesos de investigación"; que la inclusión debe ir más allá de la mera participación y "reconocer las contribuciones intelectuales de este colectivo"; y que incorporar experiencias diversas "puede contribuir a una ciencia más innovadora y socialmente relevante".
El estudio concluye que la discapacidad no debería contemplarse exclusivamente como un reto para la participación científica, sino también como "una fuente de conocimiento capaz de ampliar la comprensión de cómo se construye la ciencia y de mejorar la capacidad del sistema investigador para responder a los desafíos de una sociedad diversa".

title: Child who fell off escalator at Bishkek's shopping mall emerges from coma
content:
A child who fell off an escalator at the Vefa shopping center in Bishkek has emerged from a coma. The Bishkek City Children’s Clinical Emergency Hospital told 24.kg news agency.
The child has been transferred from intensive care to a regular ward. According to doctors, his condition is showing positive progress.
The incident occurred on the evening of August 11. A boy born in 2021 fell off an escalator at the Vefa shopping center. He was hospitalized with a severe traumatic brain injury and placed on a ventilator.

title: PMOS clinics 'good start, but more can be done'
content:
PMOS clinics 'good start, but more can be done'
- Published
The launch of a pilot health check clinic for women with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) in Jersey has been described as "a good start", but "more... can be done" for the condition, the head of a health group has said.
The metabolic condition, which affects up to one in eight women, changes how the ovaries work and was linked to infertility and weight gain, the UK's NHS said.
It was renamed PMOS from PCOS (polycystic ovary syndrome) in May to make it "more representative" of it as a whole-body condition.
The government said its trial clinic would not diagnose the condition, but help those with PMOS to get further help with it and associated conditions, including type 2 diabetes.
It added women with PMOS would need to go to their GP first to then be referred to the service, which will run at the Assisted Reproductive Unit in St Brelade from October.
Chair of PMOS Jersey Jessica Pinel said the trial clinic was in line with draft guidance from the UK's National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE), which advises annual checks so doctors can spot the wide-ranging health issues that can come with the complex condition.
Pinel was diagnosed with PMOS in 2023 after spending more than £3,100 for treatment and said times were tough financially for a lot of people.
She said: "We need to realise that cost may be a barrier to people getting support, even if the cost is going to their GP. But I think we do have to be grateful that we have had this service approved.
"Because the clinic is part of the government health system, it allows for referrals to be made into different pathways like endocrinology, dermatology, so it could actually allow for better support and reduce costs for women with PMOS."
She added: "I think it's great to see things moving forward and, for women who are newly diagnosed, there's going to be a more joined-up approach and we're now taking the long-term health consequences of PMOS more seriously."
Screening clinic nurse Corrinne Purdy said reviews for women with the condition would come with a range of checks, taking a more holistic approach.
She said: "We will see whether they're getting on alright with their medication, how they're feeling about themselves; we will do height and weight reviews, we will ask them questions about their sleep, how they're managing their condition.
"We will also speak to them about any particular fertility aspirations and how they're getting with their mental health as well."
Purdy said PMOS had been "overlooked" for a long time.
She said: "Women have been diagnosed and then not really had any sort of follow-ups... just been left to manage - whereas, actually, a lot of women struggle, particularly with some of the symptoms that come alongside it.
"PMOS is... a broad thing, and it can affect women in many different ways, and it's quite common as well, maybe more common than people think."
The government said it was providing a screening service as opposed to a treatment clinic and any women requiring specialist management for symptoms such as heavy menstrual bleeding, fertility concerns or other gynaecological conditions would be referred to the most appropriate specialist service.
It added existing waiting lists for gynaecology or surgical capacity would not be affected as additional clinical capacity had been found.
Assistant Minister for Health and Social Services Andy Howell said a lot of women "have been suffering" with PMOS and it was hoped the new trial clinic would show "that we're taking them seriously and they're not going to be dismissed".
Howell said funds for the clinic would be "managed within the budget that we have at the moment, so it's not going to cost us any more".
The Health Department was allocated £381m to spend in 2026 as part of the government's budget for 2026-2029.
The government said the clinic would offer women access to investigations including ultrasound scans and endometrial biopsies during the same visit, which could not be provided at a standard GP appointment.
"This is great that women will have somewhere to come to and perhaps have a bit more time with a specialist nurse who they can talk to," the deputy added.
Howell said Jersey would base its review on the NICE guidelines, with Pinel adding the aim of the clinic was to listen to feedback of women using the service and to feed back to the practitioners to "make sure that we are optimising the support for people with PMOS and they're getting the best possible service they can".

title: South Africa’s Eskom backtracks on proposed solar registration fines
content:
South Africa’s Eskom backtracks on proposed solar registration fines
South African utility Eskom has decided not to fine or disconnect residential customers who miss a September 30 deadline to register their small-scale embedded generation (SSEG) systems.
Eskom, alongside several municipalities, had previously warned customers with unregistered solar systems face fines of up to ZAR 30,000 ($1,846) or could have their electricity supply disconnected if they do not register in time.
Following pushback from stakeholders who have questioned Eskom’s authority to impose such a measure, the utility has now decided its imposed deadline will not trigger such penalties.
Eskom has been campaigning for all SSEG systems to be registered since early 2025 and previously extended a registration fee waiver until the end of September.
In a statement sent to pv magazine, the South African Photovoltaic Industry Association (SAPVIA) has welcomed Eskom’s decision not to proceed with the penalties while maintaining that registration, safety compliance and grid visibility remain essential as South Africa’s rooftop solar market continues to grow.
The association’s technical and policy manager, Sim Khuluse, explained that while distributors are required to keep a register of embedded generation facilities under South Africa’s Electricity Regulation Act, the requirement was never meant to be enforced through fines and disconnection threats.
“Punitive measures don’t make the grid safer; they create friction in South Africa’s energy transition at exactly the point where we need more households on board,” Khuluse added.
Beyond registration, SAPVIA says it is continuing to emphasise the importance of safety compliance via the issuance of a valid Certificate of Compliance by a registered electrical professional for every solar PV installation.
Last August, Eskom announced a renewable energy offtake program inviting large consumers to sign power purchase agreements at sites owned by the utility. The program commenced with a request for proposals covering 291 MW of solar capacity.
South Africa’s cumulative solar capacity has surpassed 10 GW, after deploying 1.6 GW last year. The country is currently undergoing a liberalization of its energy market with the phased introduction of its wholesale electricity market expected to begin early next year.

title: GTA rolls out online Financial Penalty Reduction service
content:
The General Tax Authority (GTA) has announced a new fully digital service that allows eligible taxpayers to request a reduction of financial penalties through the Dhareeba electronic platform, with decisions potentially issued within minutes of submission.
The service enables taxpayers to submit financial penalty reduction requests entirely online, with applications processed automatically by the system. According to the GTA, if an applicant meets the approved eligibility criteria, a decision may be issued within minutes, sparing taxpayers the need to visit the Authority's offices in person. The Authority confirmed that the entire process, from submission to decision, takes place through the Dhareeba platform, reflecting its broader push toward paperless, self-service tax administration.
Before applying, taxpayers are urged to ensure they meet several preliminary conditions. Applicants must have submitted all required tax returns and paid all outstanding taxes, in addition to satisfying the specific eligibility requirements set for the Financial Penalty Reduction Service. The GTA noted that the service is available to all taxpayers who meet these requirements and that each application is assessed individually against the approved eligibility criteria before a decision is reached.
The Authority also outlined important conditions that apply once a request is approved. Taxpayers have 30 days from the date of approval to pay the reduced penalty amount. If payment is not made within this period, the reduction is automatically cancelled, and the penalty reverts to its original amount, meaning applicants who delay payment risk losing the benefit entirely. Additionally, the GTA clarified that only one financial penalty reduction request may be submitted per penalty, leaving no room for repeat applications if a request is rejected or a payment deadline is missed.

title: Dozens of fans left the SCG after breaking the AFLW Swan’s crowd record before the men’s game
content:
Sydney Swans fans have shown their support for the women’s team as the fallout from the club’s continued ahead of the historic double-header at the SCG.
The AFLW Swans easily beat Essendon 9.12.66 to 6.6.42 in a morale booting victory for the club and supporters.
The playing group, bench and staff stood in the centre of the SCG to belt out the team song after a stressful week.
The Swans men’s team will face their fans at home later on Sunday afternoon in their first game since the scandal broke last Monday.
But a large part of the crowd left the SCG straight after the AFLW game.
After a tumultuous week, there was an overwhelming sense of relief for coach Colin O’Riordan after the match.
“I think I can talk personally, it’s more relief for me,” O’Riordan said.
“Again, I go back to pride and relief, they’re probably the two emotions that I have today. It’s incredible relief and pride in the group, but then relief personally that we got to win.
“To be involved in a game of that magnitude, with everything that went on, the way they conducted themselves during the week, the way they played footy, I think it epitomises everything that’s good about our footy club.”
The scandal
Players Riley Bice, Nick Blakey, Isaac Heeney, James Jordon and Chad Warner were stood down this week for breaching the club’s standards on drinking and staying out late after last Sunday’s win against Essendon in Melbourne.
The five issued a joint statement apologising for their behaviour last week.
Sydney is second on the ladder and has secured two home finals, but many angry fans are threatening to walk out after the AFLW game.
The club’s actions in banning the five players from playing for the rest of the year is separate to the police investigation.
Victoria Police have confirmed its sexual crimes squad is investigating “reports of a sexual assault” at the Pullman Hotel on Monday.
The club said on Saturday none of its players had been formally interviewed by police.
NewsWire does not suggest that any of the named players are being accused of sexual assault.
Remarks made by the club earlier in the week sparked backlash from advocates for centring the players, their careers and the upcoming AFL final, instead of the alleged victim in their language.
AFLW Swans’ ‘day of history’
The pleas from Swans officials, head coaches, the captains of the men’s and women’s teams, as well some high profile fans, were answered on Sunday with supporters coming out in force to support Sydney’s AFLW side.
The crowd of 16,672 smashed the Swans’ biggest AFLW crowd of 8264 set at their very first game, at North Sydney Oval, in 2022 and it was obvious by half-time that fans had not been deterred by the fallout of the scandal, that had embroiled the Swans players through no fault of their own.
The crowd had grown over 14,000 by three-quarter-time.
“Fans letting their feet do the talking,” Kelli Underwood remarked in the call on Fox Footy. “A day of history.”
Loud cheers rang out from the thousands in attendance whenever from the Swans’ women left or entered the ground, with multiple fans waving banners in support of women in the community.
The loudest cheer came when the record crowd was announced moments before the Swans’ women sealed the 24-point win.
“It’s amazing, we weren’t sure obviously what we were going to expecting this week to see the support that we received today is unbelievable,” Swans captain Lucy McEvoy told Fox Footy, moments after the final siren.
“Our members and fans are so tight and they know we’re united as a club and we’re better than what we were at the start of the week.”
By the early stages of the first quarter, the crowd had grown from the hundreds into the thousands with large pockets of supporters, scattered across the ground, who also found their voice in support of their girls chanting “Sydney, Sydney”, as it did at various times during the match.
A day before the game celebrities actor Luke Jacobz and Mark Beretta had urged fans not to let the actions of a handful overshadow the occasion, following pleas from club leaders AFL coach Dean Cox, captain Callum Mills, AFLW coach Colin O’Riordan and his captain Lucy McEvoy all presenting a ‘united’ front in their support of women and the club.
Essendon AFLW coach Natalie Wood praised her opponents.
“I thought Sydney Swans did a terrific job in pivoting the conversation to something really tangible and something really positive in terms of calling to the masses and telling people to come to support women, and then to support women’s football and the game,” Wood said.
‘Sydney, Sydney’
Fans decked proudly in their red and white steadily streamed through the famous gates more than breaking the Swans’ record AFLW crowd of 8264, despite the headlines that plagued the lead-up.
Sydney Swans fans lined up before gates opened, to get priority seats in the Ladies and Members stand, primarily, for the inaugural AFLW/AFL double header.
By the early stages of the first quarter, the crowd had grown significantly from the hundreds into the thousands with large pockets of supporters, scattered across the ground, who also found their voice in support of their girls chanting “Sydney, Sydney”.
The AFLW side entered the SCG to the loud cheers of a small but vocal crowd with fans creating a guard of honour for their heroes before they proceeded through the banner.
Before the game, Swans chairman Andrew Pridham addressed the club’s official AFLW function, apologising again and promising a review into the club’s culture.
“We do not excuse their behaviour. We do not ignore the impact it has had on so many people – and in particular women,” Pridham said.
“But we will seek to learn, to get better, to do better and show forgiveness.”
Swans’ initial response criticised
On Sunday, Labor MP Josh Burns became the latest politician to call out the Swans’ initial response
On Wednesday, chief executive Matthew Pavlich and chair Andrew Pridham fronted the media.
Pridham initially noted the impact on the football side was not considered by the board when it met on Tuesday night to decide the sanction.
However, he later emphasised the club’s disappointment and concern by pointing out its willingness “to effectively torpedo our season”.
Mr Burns said “the primary concern for everyone” should be the welfare of the women at the centre of the allegations.
He said the AFL was a “very powerful” institution which had the responsibility and the influence to “set culture”.
“The culture from the AFL feeds into community sport. It feeds into the national conversation,” Mr Burns said on Sunday.
“It feeds into the way and the attitudes of men and boys right around the country.
“So the focus of everyone from the very moment that these shocking allegations came forward … needs to be on ensuring that women and girls are safe, not the football finals, not minimising it with language, not minimising it with … the sorts of conversation and the sorts of statements we’ve seen, but actually making it clear that the culture and the views of people at the top are ones of zero tolerance.”
Mr Burns pointed to a “correction” made by the Swans in its language around the alleged sexual assault but said he would not “congratulate” the club for “realising the focus … should have been on the alleged victims, not footy finals or footy games”.
“The work that we all need to do is ensure that those who are in positions of leadership and power set the culture and the tone to make sure that we are all focusing on what’s appropriate,” he said.
On Friday, Swans team coach Dean Cox and captain Callum Mills issued an apology, saying their thoughts remained “with everyone affected, particularly the women involved”.
“All women deserve to feel safe and respected,” they said.

title: «المربوعة» في ليبيا... مجلس تتوارثه الأجيال ويتسع دوره السياسي
content:
في شرق ليبيا وغربها، لا تزال «المربوعة» حاضرة في بيوت تتوارثها أجيال، بوصفها غرفة لاستقبال الضيوف ومجلساً اجتماعياً يجمع شيوخ القبائل والشباب، قبل أن تتسع وظيفتها لتشمل الشأن العام، وتعزز حضورها في «شبكات النفوذ السياسي والمسلح» منذ سقوط نظام الزعيم الراحل معمر القذافي في 2011.
وفي مدينة سلوق بشرق البلاد، رصدت «الشرق الأوسط» جانباً من أجواء هذه المجالس، حيث اجتمع شيوخ وأعيان وشباب وموظفون داخل غرفة استقبال ملحقة بمنزل أحدهم.
وتوزعت الأحاديث في أمسية ليلية بين مشروعات «إعادة الإعمار»، والتحسن النسبي في الخدمات بمدن الشرق، والمخاوف من استمرار التعقيدات الأمنية والسياسية في غرب ليبيا، فضلاً عن قضايا اجتماعية ومعيشية وأحوال الناس اليومية.
ومن ثم لا تبدو «المربوعة» مجرد غرفة للضيافة، بل إن لها، حسب باحثين اجتماعيين، مكانتها بوصفها مساحة اجتماعية في البيوت الليبية تواصلت عبر أجيال، وظلت تؤدي دوراً في جمع الناس وتبادل الآراء، رغم تغير أنماط البناء وتصميم المنازل.
ويترسخ هذا التصور في دراسة أكاديمية تحدثت عن أن التطور المعماري في البيوت الليبية العصرية لم يقترب من وظيفة «المربوعة» الاجتماعية، إذ لا يزال الليبيون يخصصون لها مساحة مستقلة وواسعة، حسب عواطف فرج بوجلدين، الباحثة في كلية الفنون والعمارة بجامعة درنة.
ولم يكن حضور «المربوعة» في الشأن العام وليد مرحلة ما بعد 2011، وإن ظل دورها السياسي قبل ذلك محدوداً مقارنة بما آلت إليه وظائفها لاحقاً.
فقبل «ثورة» فبراير (شباط) 2011، ارتبطت مجالسها بمعالجة المشكلات الاجتماعية، والتدخل في حل النزاعات الأهلية، والمشاركة في المناسبات الاجتماعية وجمع التبرعات.
كما كان لها حضور سياسي محدود تمثل في المشاركة في اختيار ممثلي المدن والقرى في المؤتمرات الشعبية الأساسية، التي كانت تؤدي دوراً شبيهاً بالمجالس المحلية في الوقت الراهن، وفق حديث عضو مجلس النواب فهمي التواتي لـ«الشرق الأوسط».
ومع سقوط نظام القذافي وما أعقبه من ضعف مؤسسات الدولة والانقسام السياسي والأمني، اتسعت وظائف هذه المجالس، فتحولت في مناطق عدة إلى فضاءات غير رسمية للنقاش والتشاور والمصالحة، وأصبحت جزءاً من شبكات العلاقات المحلية.
ويفسر رئيس «المنظمة الليبية للتنمية السياسية»، جمال الفلاح، جانباً من هذا التحول انطلاقاً من تجربة عايشها خلال الفوضى الأمنية التي أعقبت 2011، حين كانت بعض الميليشيات تقتحم اجتماعات سياسية.
ويشير في حديثه إلى «الشرق الأوسط» إلى أن «المربوعة» وفرت في بعض الحالات مساحة أكثر أمناً لعقد اجتماعات تتعلق بالدستور أو الترتيبات السياسية، إذ كان اقتحامها يعد خرقاً للأعراف الاجتماعية.
ويرى الفلاح أن مجالس «المربوعة» أدت أيضاً دور «رمانة الميزان» خلال فترات غياب الدولة، عندما عادت القبيلة إلى الواجهة لتؤدي أدواراً أوسع في ضبط التوازنات واحتواء الخلافات.
كما لعبت هذه المجالس دوراً في المصالحات المحلية، إذ استضافت لقاءات بين قبائل ومدن متخاصمة، وساعدت في مناقشة قضايا تتعلق بوقف الثأر وفتح الطرق وعودة المهجرين وتسوية النزاعات.
ويستند هذا الدور إلى المكانة الاجتماعية التي يتمتع بها شيوخ القبائل والأعيان، وإلى الأعراف المحلية التي تمنح التفاهمات التي تنشأ داخل هذه المجالس وزناً في مجتمعاتها.
ولا يقتصر حضور «المربوعة» على المصالحات، إذ يشير التواتي إلى أنها أصبحت في بعض المناطق مساحة للتشاور والتوافق بشأن المرشحين في الاستحقاقات الانتخابية.
ويمتد حضور «المربوعة» إلى مدن وقرى عدة شرقاً وغرباً، وإن اختلفت طبيعة دورها من منطقة إلى أخرى. ويقول التواتي إن حضورها «لا يزال أكثر وضوحاً خارج مراكز المدن الكبرى».
وفي طرابلس، تراجع حضورها التقليدي داخل قلب العاصمة لتحل الفنادق والمكاتب واللقاءات الخاصة والرسمية محلها في كثير من الأحيان، لكنه يؤكد استمرارها في الضواحي.
ولا يعني تراجع شكلها التقليدي، وفق التواتي، اختفاء دورها، إذ يمكن أن تكون جلساتها تمهيداً اجتماعياً لما يجري لاحقاً في الفنادق والمكاتب من لقاءات سياسية، وربما تفاهمات أو صفقات سياسية.
ويضيف التواتي أن كثيراً من التفاهمات التي تناقَش في الأماكن المغلقة قد تسبقها مشاورات اجتماعية داخل «المربوعة»، خصوصاً في المدن والقرى التي لا تزال تحتفظ بهذا النمط من التواصل.
ويرصد سياسيون وبرلمانيون ومحللون اتساع توظيف «المربوعة» لبناء العلاقات وتوطيد النفوذ الاجتماعي والسياسي، حتى مع تغير شكلها في بعض المناطق واتخاذها طابعاً أكثر عصرية.
وفي غرب ليبيا، تظهر بين حين وآخر صور ولقطات لقيادات سياسية وأمنية وعسكرية خلال جلسات داخل مجالس اجتماعية؛ كما احتضنت «المربوعة» لقاءات لرئيس حكومة «الوحدة الوطنية» المؤقت عبد الحميد الدبيبة في منزله مع قادة اجتماعيين وقبليين.
أما في شرق البلاد، فقد احتضنت «المربوعة» لقاءات قبل عدة أعوام بين سلطات شرق ليبيا وأعضاء في مجلسي النواب والدولة، بهدف ترطيب الأجواء والحصول على قاعدة شعبية لمشروعات الإعمار، حسب مصدر برلماني فضّل عدم الكشف عن هويته.
لكن اتساع الدور السياسي لـ«المربوعة» يثير نقاشاً حول حدود تأثير المؤسسات الاجتماعية غير الرسمية في إدارة الشأن العام، وسط تحذيرات من تحولها إلى بديل عن مؤسسات الدولة.

title: Team finds way to ‘wake up’ tired immune cells
content:
Researchers have found a way to wake up tired immune cells..
It’s like a shot of espresso for “exhausted” immune systems—a discovery that could restore the body’s defenses against cancer and infection.
For decades, scientists have accepted that the immune system naturally weakens with age. Georgia Tech biomedical engineer Ankur Singh wasn’t convinced.
Then the COVID-19 pandemic made the stakes impossible to ignore.
Singh says that as older adults struggled to recover from COVID, he recognized the same pattern he had been studying for years in cancer: an aging immune system that could no longer respond the way it once had.
“It pointed us back to the immune system,” says Singh, a faculty member in the Parker H. Petit Institute for Bioengineering and Bioscience and director of the Center for Immunoengineering at Georgia Tech.
“Looking at the number of people who suffered from Covid, and how poorly the immune system was prepared to fight a new infection, it became clear this was a fundamental problem.”
A lot of aging research, he notes, “focuses on the brain or physical health. But immune aging is central to so many of these problems, and there are far fewer solutions. Now we’re asking whether we can repair some of its root causes.”
In a study published in Cell Biomaterials, Singh and his collaborators, led by PhD student Zhonghao Dai, set out to answer that question.
The team focused on T cells, the immune system’s frontline defenders against viruses, abnormal cells, and the earliest signs of cancer.
T cells protect us by responding to new infections and eliminating dangerous cells before they can take hold. As we age, the body produces fewer fresh T cells, and older ones become less effective.
“They’re exhausted,” Singh says.
He wanted to know whether aging immune cells could recover some of what they had lost. To restore aging immune cells, researchers first have to deliver new biological instructions into T cells. Existing methods have made that difficult, often damaging fragile cells or failing to reach enough of them to be effective.
Using microscopic silicon nanowires, Singh and his team delivered the instructions into more than 90% of aging T cells without damaging them. The goal wasn’t to reverse aging. It was to restore enough of the cells’ lost function to allow them to behave more like younger immune cells.
“These signals act like instructions,” Singh says. “They help reset the cells’ internal programs.”
A scanning electron micrograph from the laboratory of Ankur Singh and Zhonghao Dai shows aged human T cells resting on top of a bed of microscopic silicon nanowires, which are engineered to interact directly with the cells and restore their youthful function.
Much like a cup of coffee, the treatment invigorated exhausted immune cells, helping them respond more like younger ones. The treated cells became more active. They multiplied and regained their ability to attack infected and cancerous cells.
“What surprised me most was that we only needed to fix four or five of these genes to bring T cells closer to a younger state,” Singh says.
The team then tested immune cells from healthy older adults, cancer survivors, and patients living with cancer. “We started seeing improvement in their T cell function,” Singh says. “That’s when we knew this could work across different conditions and across different people.”
The results held across each group, giving him confidence that the approach could work far more broadly than the team first imagined.
“This technique has wide applications: cancer, infection, inflammatory bowel disease, autoimmunity,” Singh says. “They’re ready to fight whatever is invading your body. You’ll respond better to vaccines. You’ll simply live a healthier life and get sick less often.”
For now, the effects last about two weeks. Singh and his team are working to make them last longer.
The body’s cells still grow older. But they may not have to act like it.
Additional coauthors are from Georgia Tech and Emory University.
This research was supported by the National Institutes of Health, the National Science Foundation, the Curci Foundation, and the Carl Ring Family Endowment.

title: Valikhан Turekhanov: “The President cannot be a member of a party, and his relatives cannot hold state positions”
content:
One of the outcomes of the transformations in Kazakhstan’s political system was the limitation of the president’s powers: the head of state cannot be a member of a political party, and his relatives cannot hold positions in the state power system. This was stated by Kazakhstan’s Ambassador to Tajikistan Valikhan Turekhanов at a briefing on August 28 in Dushanbe.
The diplomat reported on the results of the first elections to the country’s new unicameral parliament and explained in detail the changes that occurred in Kazakhstan’s political system following the constitutional reform.
From the “Super-Presidential” Model to a New System of Power
On August 23, Kazakhstan held the first elections for deputies to the new unicameral parliament — the Majilis. According to the ambassador, these elections were a continuation of the reforms that began in 2022. According to Turekhanов, the starting point for the reforms was the constitutional referendum of June 5, 2022.
According to him, 33 articles of Kazakhstan’s Constitution were amended at that time. The main direction was the redistribution of powers between branches of government and a gradual move away from the “super-presidential” model of power.
Among the changes, he highlighted several restrictions for the head of state:
- the president cannot be a member of a political party;
- the president cannot have relatives in the state power system;
- certain presidential powers were limited.
The ambassador separately addressed changes related to natural resources.
According to him, following the reforms, land, subsoil resources, water, minerals, and other natural resources became the property of the people of Kazakhstan, with the state managing them.
How Kazakhstan Transitioned to a Unicameral Parliament
Following the political reforms of 2022, Kazakhstan entered a new constitutional phase. According to Valikhan Turekhanов, on March 15, 2026, a new Constitution was adopted at a republican referendum, which consolidated the transition to a unicameral parliament — the Majilis. On July 1, the new Constitution came into force, after which the powers of the previous bicameral parliament ended.
On August 23, elections were held for deputies to the new Majilis. Seven political parties participated in them. Following the voting results, five parties entered parliament: “Adalet” received 110 seats, “Auyl” — 10 seats, “Respublika” — 9 seats, “Ak Zhol” and the National Social Democratic Party — 8 seats each. A total of 145 deputies entered the new composition of the Majilis.
The elections were monitored by 797 international observers from 41 countries and 13 international organizations. In the new composition of the Majilis, 49 women out of 145 deputies will work, which constitutes approximately 33% of the total number of parliamentarians.
Explaining the transition to a single chamber of parliament, the ambassador noted that previously, the passage of certain laws could take more time due to going through two chambers.
“One bill could circulate between the two chambers,” said Turekhanов, explaining the necessity of the new model.
According to him, the new system should make the legislative process faster and more transparent.
How the Elections Took Place in Dushanbe
At the polling station at Kazakhstan’s embassy in Dushanbe, there were 111 citizens on the voter rolls. 88 people participated in the voting, with a turnout of almost 80%. The “Adilet” party received the majority of votes — 63 votes.
Tajik observers also participated in the elections. The Tajikistan delegation was headed by the Chairman of the Central Election Commission Bakhtiyar Khudoyorzoda. Valikhan Turekhanов expressed gratitude to his Tajik colleagues for their participation in international observation and noted the importance of support from neighboring countries during the period of important political reforms.
According to the ambassador, Tajik observers positively assessed the organization of the voting and the conditions created for citizens to participate in the electoral process.

title: Robot-assisted surgery shows clinical advantages over laparoscopic surgery for gastric cancer
content:
Surgery remains the primary curative treatment for gastric cancer, with laparoscopic gastrectomy (LG) established as a standard minimally invasive approach. While LG offers faster recovery than open surgery, it remains technically demanding because surgeons must operate within a confined space using rigid instruments that can amplify hand tremors.
Robotic gastrectomy (RG) was developed to overcome these limitations by providing greater precision, enhanced dexterity and improved visualization. Although RG has become increasingly common, whether it delivers meaningful clinical benefits over conventional laparoscopic surgery in routine practice has remained uncertain.
In Japan, RG was approved for national insurance coverage in 2018, followed by regulatory changes that expanded access to robotic surgery and increased the number of surgeons qualified to perform the procedure. Five years later, researchers sought to determine whether these advances had translated into better outcomes for patients undergoing gastric cancer surgery.
Their findings were published in the journal Gastric Cancer.
The study was led by Professor Susumu Shibasaki from the Department of Surgery, Fujita Health University–Okazaki Medical Center, Japan, together with Dr. Koichi Suda from Fujita Health University, Dr. Hideki Endo from the University of Tokyo, Dr. Ken Shirabe from Gunma University and colleagues. The study was conducted with the support of the Japanese Gastric Cancer Association.
To answer this question, the researchers analyzed data from Japan's National Clinical Database, identifying patients who underwent minimally invasive distal gastrectomy (DG) or total gastrectomy (TG) between January 2023 and December 2024.
Using propensity score matching to account for differences between patients, they compared 9,743 matched pairs of robotic and laparoscopic DG cases, as well as 1,617 matched pairs of robotic and laparoscopic TG cases.
"RG has become broadly integrated into routine clinical practice across Japan. Under these contemporary conditions, it remains essential to clarify whether RG offers tangible clinical advantages over LG," says Prof. Shibasaki.
The analysis showed that robotic procedures consistently required longer operating times than laparoscopic surgery. On average, robotic DG took approximately 50 minutes longer than laparoscopic surgery, while robotic TG required nearly 70 additional minutes.
Despite the longer procedures, robotic surgery demonstrated several important clinical advantages. For both DG and TG, robotic surgery resulted in 33–40% less blood loss, a 50–65% lower likelihood of conversion to open surgery and shorter postoperative hospital stays than laparoscopic surgery.
Among patients undergoing DG, robotic surgery also reduced serious postoperative complications and intra-abdominal infections compared with laparoscopic surgery.
"Although the absolute magnitudes of these differences were small, the consistent benefits across multiple perioperative outcomes indicate that RG may achieve a level of minimal invasiveness beyond LG, which itself is a highly refined minimally invasive approach," says Shibasaki, adding that these benefits were evident even in a large and diverse nationwide cohort.
The findings also suggest that RG has continued to improve since its introduction into routine care. Compared with an earlier nationwide study conducted before national insurance coverage was approved in 2018, the current analysis found better outcomes following robotic surgery.
The researchers believe these improvements reflect ongoing advances in robotic technology, greater surgical experience and expanded training opportunities over the past several years.
The benefits, however, were not identical across all procedures. While robotic DG significantly reduced major postoperative complications, robotic TG did not show a significant improvement in this primary outcome compared with laparoscopic surgery.
According to the researchers, TG remains a more technically demanding procedure, and surgeons perform it less frequently, limiting opportunities to gain experience with robotic techniques.
Looking ahead, the researchers believe continued technological innovation and broader adoption of robotic surgery will further improve outcomes for patients with gastric cancer.
"Over the next five to 10 years, these findings are expected to accelerate the widespread adoption of robotic surgery. As a result, more patients will have access to safer, higher-quality surgical care, leading to better recovery, fewer complications, and improved overall outcomes," he concludes.

title: 4 women from GB successfully summit Spantik
content: GILGIT: Four women mountaineers from Gilgit-Baltistan, joined by a Romanian climber and a male mountaineer from Punjab, successfully summited 7,027-metre Spantik Peak without the assistance of high-altitude porters, marking an inspiring achievement amid challenging conditions in the region. The Alpine Club of Pakistan confirmed that the four-member local women’s team reached the summit and safely returned to Skardu on Monday. The successful climbers were Shama Baqir and Samana Rahim of Shimshal Valley, Zooni Aslam of Gulmit Valley in Gojal, Upper Hunza, and Zaiba Batool Shigri of Shigar district. Bismah Hassan of Lahore was also part of the expedition but returned around 250 metres below the summit after experiencing a health issue. Bad weather hampers efforts to bring to Skardu bodies of Dr Asma Mushtaq and American climber Sarah Mallory Geis Alpine Club of Pakistan General Secretary Ayaz Shigri told Dawn that the women reached the summit either a day before or on the same day that climber Dr Asma Mushtaq died while descending from the mountain. He said weather conditions had been favourable at the peak before Friday, but subsequent deterioration created difficulties for rescue and recovery operations. The expedition also featured Alexandra Visan of Romania, who, despite battling cancer, successfully climbed Spantik and descended safely. Her expedition was organised by Broad Boy Adventures, owned by Pakistani mountaineer Shehroze Kashif. Zaiba Batool from Shigar waves the Pakistani flag. —Dawn In a social media post, Mr Kashif said Ms Visan was accompanied by local high-altitude porter Ali Ameen of Shigar. He described her achievement as a story of perseverance, saying some climbs are about finding the strength to continue when life itself becomes the mountain. Punjab climber Ayyan Adeel also summited Spantik. According to Mr Kashif, the attempt was notable because Ayyan became the youngest climber to summit the peak without high-altitude porter support, carrying his own equipment with assistance from fellow expedition members Awais Choudary and Talha Khalid. While the successful summits brought encouragement to the mountaineering community, deteriorating weather has continued to hamper efforts to bring to Skardu the body of Dr Asma Mushtaq, who died at an altitude of around 6,250 metres on Thursday while descending from the Spantik summit. Her body remains at Camp 3. Mr Shigri said a six-member team of high-altitude porters reached Camp 2 on Sunday and attempted to proceed towards Camp 3. However, heavy rain and snowfall forced the team to turn back to Camp 2. Weather conditions are expected to improve on Tuesday, after which rescuers will make another attempt to bring Dr Mushtaq’s body down to base camp. Pakistan Army helicopters are then expected to airlift the body to Skardu. Bad weather has also prevented helicopter operations at 8,047-metre Broad Peak, where the body of American climber Sarah Mallory Geis remains at the base camp awaiting airlift. title: Uber y la fintech R2 fortalecen alianza en Perú para ofrecer financiamiento
content:
Uber Technologies Inc. y R2, fintech especializada en soluciones de financiamiento digital, fortalecen su alianza en Perú para ampliar el acceso al crédito entre los socios conductores de la plataforma. Como parte del acuerdo, los conductores podrán recibir ofertas de financiamiento directamente a través de la aplicación Uber para Conductor, sin necesidad de realizar trámites presenciales.
Perú se ha convertido en el mercado de mayor aceleración del programa de financiamiento de Uber y R2 en la región, según R2. La compañía señala que este comportamiento responde a una demanda de capital entre miles de conductores que generan ingresos diariamente mediante la aplicación y que enfrentan barreras para acceder al crédito tradicional.
En el mercado peruano, el monto promedio de los préstamos otorgados bajo este programa se ubica alrededor de los US$200, mientras que el plazo promedio de pago es de aproximadamente cinco meses. El financiamiento está orientado a atender necesidades inmediatas de los socios conductores, como cubrir imprevistos o invertir en herramientas vinculadas con su actividad.
Uber y R2: financiamiento a socios conductores
El acceso al crédito se gestiona directamente desde la aplicación de Uber para Conductor. Las ofertas son preaprobadas a partir del historial de actividad del socio dentro de la plataforma, por lo que no es necesario presentar documentación adicional ni realizar trámites presenciales para acceder al financiamiento.
El esquema de pago también está vinculado a la actividad que realizan los conductores en Uber. El préstamo se cancela automáticamente mediante un porcentaje de las ganancias obtenidas por los viajes, permitiendo que los pagos se ajusten al flujo de ingresos generado por cada usuario.
La operación representa la primera colaboración conjunta de Uber y R2 en Perú. La alianza entre ambas compañías comenzó a inicios de 2025 en otros mercados de la región, inicialmente con soluciones de financiamiento dirigidas a restaurantes que operan mediante Uber Eats. Ahora, el acuerdo incorpora a los socios conductores dentro de este modelo.
Para Uber, la iniciativa busca ampliar las oportunidades económicas de sus socios conductores mediante financiamiento integrado en la plataforma que utilizan para generar ingresos. El avance del programa en Perú coincide con la expansión de R2 en América Latina, tras la inversión estratégica de Ant International para acelerar el acceso al crédito de pequeñas y medianas empresas mediante tecnología, análisis de riesgo y modelos de financiamiento embebido.
Planes de crecimiento de Uber en Perú
En entrevista con Gestión, Ángela Mendoza, gerente general de Uber para Perú, Colombia y Ecuador, señaló que 2026 será un año de consolidación para Uber en Perú, tras la expansión hacia nuevas ciudades. La estrategia tendrá tres ejes: impulsar la adopción de la aplicación, fortalecer su vínculo con el turismo y promover la educación sobre el uso de plataformas digitales de movilidad.
La compañía revisará su portafolio según las necesidades de cada mercado. Uber opera actualmente en cerca de 30 ciudades y evalúa incorporar servicios como Uber Comfort, Uber Black y mototaxi, además de UberX. Ica, Huancayo, Tacna, Cusco, Arequipa y Cajamarca figuran entre las ciudades con mayor potencial, donde la plataforma registró crecimientos de tres dígitos durante su expansión y ahora apunta a mantener tasas de doble dígito.
Uber también busca crecer mediante alianzas vinculadas al turismo, aerolíneas y eventos, además de impulsar Uber para negocios, segmento que avanza a doble dígito. Lima concentra cerca del 50% de la facturación de la compañía en el país, mientras que Perú, junto con Colombia, se encuentra entre los 15 mercados más importantes de Uber en Latinoamérica.

title: Impact of Metformin Plus Lifestyle Intervention Compared With Lifestyle Intervention Alone on Prediabetes Remission in Participants With Impaired Glucose Regulation: The China DPP Study.
content: Prediabetes affects 35% of Chinese adults and is associated with increased risks of cardiovascular disease and mortality. However, findings are inconsistent on the effects of lifestyle and pharmacological interventions in the prediabetes population achieving remission. This analysis aimed to compare the effects of metformin plus lifestyle intervention versus lifestyle intervention alone for prediabetes remission. This was a secondary analysis of the China Diabetes Prevention Program (CDPP), a multicentre unblinded randomised controlled trial of 1678 participants aged 18-70 years with impaired glucose regulation from 43 hospitals across China (NCT03441750). Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) using block randomisation stratified by glucose status (impaired fasting glucose or impaired glucose tolerance), presence of hypertension and use of anti-hypertensive medication. They received either metformin plus lifestyle intervention or lifestyle intervention alone for 2 years. The primary outcome was prediabetes remission rate. During a median follow-up of 2.03 years, remission was achieved in 262/831 (31.5%) (138/396 men; 124/435 women) participants in the metformin plus lifestyle group versus 213/847 (25.1%) (106/397 men; 107/450 women) in the lifestyle alone group, with similar effects across subgroups. After adjusting for baseline characteristics, addition of metformin increased the rate of remission (HR 1.39, 95% CI 1.16-1.67, p < 0.001). Higher baseline HbA1c was associated with lower remission rates (HR 0.23, 95% CI 0.18-0.29, p < 0.001). Adding metformin to a lifestyle intervention significantly improved prediabetes remission rates over lifestyle intervention alone in Chinese adults with impaired glucose regulation. This may be an effective approach for prediabetes management.

title: Knowledge Nugget | Tolling without barriers: India’s shift to multi-lane free flow
content:
Story continues below this ad



2. The first Digital Local Pass facility was launched in July 2026 at the Mundka-Bakkarwala toll plaza on Urban Extension Road-II (UER-II) in Delhi.
3. The digital local pass facility is integrated with DigiLocker and VAHAN, which retrieve the commuter’s address to verify the 20-km radius condition, vehicle details and the linked FASTag to issue the pass. This removes the need for manual documentation and physical verification.
4. While the digital local pass is part of the government’s Digital India project, its implementation picked pace after the NHAI started implementing the MLFF system at its toll plazas.
5. The barrier-less tolling system is currently operational at six toll plazas, namely Choryasi, Mundaka, Daulatpura, Gharaunda, Manoharpur, and Shahjahanpur.
What is a multi-lane free flow tolling system?
Story continues below this ad
6. The MLFF system removes the need for boom barriers and vehicles to stop for toll collection. Instead, high-performance Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) readers and Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras read the FASTag and Vehicle Registration Number (VRN).
7. According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, the MLFF is projected to be implemented across all four-lane and above national highways and expressways by March 2029.
8. Currently, there are around 1,100 user fee plazas or toll plazas across the country, out of which over 450 toll plazas were constructed in the last five years.
What were the enabling steps behind the implementation of MLFF?
9. The NHAI took a series of decisions that created an enabling platform for the rollout of MLFF. This was done to create a robust legal framework so that commuters do not find loopholes to avoid toll charges.
Story continues below this ad
10. One of the earliest decisions was mandating the use of High Security Registration Plates (HSRP). This was to ensure that specially designed ANPR cameras can read number plates.
11. The other key decision was “One Vehicle, One FASTag”. It stopped the usage of a single FASTag for multiple vehicles or linking multiple FASTags to a particular vehicle.
12. In March, MoRTH issued new National Highway Fee rules to deal with cases of unpaid user fees, meaning the vehicle passed the toll but did not pay. It says that in such cases, commuters will have to pay double the applicable toll amount at the respective toll plaza. However, if it is paid within 72 hours, only the original user fee will apply.
13. An e-notice will be issued with the vehicle details, the date and location of occurrence and the user fee payable. The rules also provide for a grievance redressal mechanism, where a vehicle owner/driver dissatisfied with the e-notice can challenge it within 72 hours. If the challenge is not disposed of within five days by the tolling agency, the claim for the unpaid user fee shall lapse.
Story continues below this ad
14. The rules also paved the way for integrating the National Electronic Toll Collection system with the National Vehicle Registry (VAHAN) for enforcement measures and the realisation of unpaid user fees.
15. Apart from this, in February 2026, NHAI issued a direction to all FASTag-issuing banks to immediately validate VRNs or license plate numbers linked to the FASTags they have issued. The agency also directed banks to blacklist FASTags found linked to incorrect or invalid VRNs.
16. The direction was issued because, in the absence of human intervention in the toll deduction system in MLFF at the toll gate, a mismatch in the VRN linked to the FASTag could see commuters pass without paying the fee.
What is FASTag?
1. FASTag is an electronic toll collection system managed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) and the NHAI. A FASTag sticker is usually pasted on the windscreen of a car. It was launched in 2014 as a pilot project and made mandatory at every toll plaza in the country in 2021.
Story continues below this ad
2. It uses Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technology to communicate with scanners installed at toll plazas. Once the car crosses a toll plaza, the requisite toll amount is automatically deducted from a bank account or a prepaid wallet linked to the FASTag.
3. RFID is a wireless tracking system that consists of tags and readers. Radio waves are used to communicate information/identity of objects or people to nearby readers – devices that can be hand-held or built into fixed positions like poles or buildings.
4. The tags can carry encrypted information, serial numbers and short descriptions. There are also high-memory tags like the ones designed for use in the aviation industry.
5. There are different types of RFID tags: Passive tags, semi-passive tags, and active tags. Active RFIDs use their own power source, mostly batteries. Active tags can ping information every few seconds like beacons, or they can get activated when a reader is in the proximity.
Story continues below this ad
6. Passive RFIDs, on the other hand, are activated through the reader using the electromagnetic energy it transmits. This is enough power for the tag to transmit information back to the reader. Active tags have a longer read range, around 300 ft, compared to passive tags.
7. FASTag uses passive RFID tags. Semi-passive tags comprise an internal circuit with a power source, but rely on the radio waves received from the reader to transmit the response.
8. RFID tags use an integrated circuit and an antenna to communicate with a reader using radio waves at several different frequencies – low frequency (LF), high frequency (HF), and ultra-high frequency (UHF). The message sent back by the tag in the form of radio waves is translated into data and analysed by the host computer system.
BEYOND THE NUGGET: GNSS- based tolling system
1. Under the GNSS, the toll collection system works with the help of satellites and on-board unit (OBU) fitted vehicles.
Story continues below this ad
2. The movement of the vehicle will be tracked by satellite, and users will pay toll only for the distance they have travelled, rather than the fixed amounts for set distances that they pay now.
3. For GNSS to work, owners have to get a non-transferable “on-board unit” (OBU) fitted in their vehicles.
4. The Apex Committee and High-Level Empowered Committee consisting of experts from Industry and Academia, in view of security and privacy considerations, breach and overall operational control, had recommended further deliberations for Satellite based Tolling in March, 2025.
5. After much deliberation, it was proposed to proceed with corridor/stretch-based projects for ANPR FASTag system (AFS)-based Barrier Less Free Flow tolling.
Post Read Questions
With reference to the Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) tolling system, consider the following statements:
1. MLFF eliminates the requirement of a physical toll barrier by identifying vehicles while they are in motion.
2. Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) and Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) can together provide alternative means of identifying a vehicle in an MLFF system.
3. The implementation of MLFF makes High Security Registration Plates (HSRP) unnecessary, since the vehicle can be identified solely through its FASTag.
4. Integration of FASTag-related information with the VAHAN database can facilitate recovery of unpaid user fees.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
(a) 1, 2 and 4 only
(b) 1 and 3 only
(c) 2, 3 and 4 only
(d) 1, 2, 3 and 4
Answer: (a)

Saint-Louis : 456 candidats à l’émigration irrégulière secourus en une semaine
La Marine nationale a porté secours, samedi 22 août 2026, à une pirogue transportant 210 candidats à l’émigration irrégulière au large de Saint-Louis. Plusieurs d’entre eux se trouvaient dans un état de santé jugé préoccupant.
