title: Kristo Asafo Mission donates cash, clothes to Essumeja community
content:
Residents of Essumeja in the Bekwai Municipality of the Ashanti Region have benefited from the benevolence of the Kristo Asafo Mission.
Led by their new leader, Nana Kwadwo Safo Akofena I, the Church last Thursday presented 1,500 pieces of clothing to sections of the community at a grand presentation ceremony at Essumeja, the hometown of the founder of the church.
The donation of cash, in addition to the clothes, forms part of the annual ritual of the late Apostle Safo to orphanages, prisons and members of the Essumeja community to mark his birthday (August 26).
Traditional leaders and elders received 300 pieces of clothes while family members of the late Apostle Kwadwo Safo got 230 pieces of clothes.
Police personnel and health workers received 90 and 15 pieces, respectively, with 600 pieces going to the general public and community members, while Elders of the Asantemanso enclave got 10 pieces.
Nana Safo Akofena, accompanied by Lawyer Owusu Badu, Council of Elders and Pastors of the Church, assured the community that the donation and presentation would be sustained to the memory of his late father.
He said the Church will be fully established in the community to consolidate the mission and vision of the founder.
Earlier, Nana Akofena and his entourage had called on the Paramount Chief of the Essumeja Traditional Area, Nana Okyere Kusi Ntrama.
The Kristo Asafo Mission leader pledged to strengthen the already healthy relationship between the church, his family members and the community. He also promised to contribute to the development of the community.
The Essumejamanhene commended the leadership of the church for their generosity and called for unity among the family and children of the late industrialist, renowned pastor, inventor and entrepreneur, in order to protect his legacy.
From Oswald P. Freiku, Essumeja

title: Comunidade se une e paga salários de funcionários de pizzaria tradicional destruída por incêndio
content:
Comunidade se une e paga salários de funcionários de pizzaria tradicional destruída por incêndio
Moradores e clientes se uniram para ajudar a pagar os salários dos funcionários de uma pizzaria que funciona há mais de 50 anos, foi atingida por um incêndio e teve que fechar as portas. A comunidade de Minneapolis, nos Estados Unidos, arrecadou milhares de dólares para garantir que a casa volte a funcionar e os funcionários possam se manter até lá.
A mobilização começou depois que a Jakeeno’s Pizza & Pasta, que passou de pai para filhas – e é administrada pelas irmãs Patty e Amy Keegan – foi atingida por um incêndio em 11 de julho, no sul de Minneapolis, no estado de Minnesota. “Queremos eles de volta. Nós os valorizamos. É terrível que tenham perdido o trabalho por causa disso, então estamos tentando manter todo mundo amparado”, disse ela à CBS Minnesota.
A pizzaria é tão querida na região que o empresário Bob Tinsley criou uma campanha de arrecadação no GoFundMe e já conseguiu arrecadar US$ 22,6 mil (mais de R$ 116 mil) para ajudar cozinheiros, garçons, bartenders e outros trabalhadores a atravessar o período sem renda.
Tradição de mais de 50 anos
A Jakeeno’s Pizza & Pasta funciona há mais de cinco décadas em Minneapolis. É um restaurante familiar.
A pizzaria foi fundada em 1975 por Jack e Carol Keegan e, anos depois, passou a ser administrada pelas filhas Patty e Amy.
Ao longo da história, o restaurante enfrentou momentos difíceis, como a crise financeira, a pandemia de Covid-19 e os impactos dos protestos que aconteceram na região após a morte de George Floyd, por policiais.

O incêndio
O fogo atingiu o telhado da pizzaria na manhã de 11 de julho. Os bombeiros precisaram abrir diferentes pontos da cobertura para controlar as chamas.
O restaurante estava vazio naquele momento e ninguém ficou ferido. Mesmo assim, fumaça e destroços atingiram áreas internas e obrigaram o estabelecimento a suspender as atividades enquanto passa por reparos.
Agora, quem ajuda a pizzaria a atravessar mais um momento complicado são justamente os clientes e vizinhos que frequentam o local há anos.
Manter a equipe unida
A notícia boa é que as obras da reforma estão em andamento.
Patty Keegan contou que a principal preocupação hoje é conseguir manter a equipe unida para quando o restaurante reabrir.
Além das doações, moradores também podem apoiar o negócio comprando molhos e pizzas congeladas da marca, vendidos em mercados e cooperativas locais.

title: La explosión del 'Slow Travel': "Ir con pulserita no se puede asociar a la calma, si acaso a mayor control, y un viaje debe ser todo lo contrario"
content:
McDonald's no hubiera decidido, en 1986, inaugurar su primer establecimiento en Roma, posiblemente este reportaje no existiría. Si la empresa no hubiera decidido entonces que llegaba el momento de expandir su fast food por Europa, empezando por la cuna de la cocina mediterránea, seguramente Carlo Petrini, que falleció con 76 años el pasado mayo, no habría sacado adelante el movimiento Slow Food, que empezó con una cacerolada en Piazza di Spagna en la que los participantes ofrecían platos de spaghetti, penne y otras viandas para evitar la inauguración del local.
Los Big Mac siguen sirviéndose en el mismo lugar, en pleno centro histórico de la ciudad. Pero el contrapunto ejercido por Petrini permitió fundar el movimiento global Slow Food, que defiende una alimentación «buena, limpia y justa» y se opone a la vida acelerada (hoy mucho más que en 1986), a través del respeto al medio ambiente y el trato digno a los productores. A lo largo de las siguientes décadas, el fenómeno se fue trasladando a otros aspectos de la vida. La lentitud se fue colando en la moda (Slow Fashion), el urbanismo (Slow Cities) y la salud (Slow Health o Slow Medicine).Slow Living, en definitiva.
Mientras que el Slow Travel, el fenómeno de viajar más lento y de manera más consciente, tardó un poco en llegar. Por una razón muy sencilla y que todo el mundo ha notado en sus carnes: llegan las vacaciones y lo que queremos es disfrutar al máximo y a la voz de ya. La lentitud no suele entrar en los planes: prisa por buscar el vuelo, prisa por llegar al aeropuerto, al hotel, a la playa, al restaurante de moda y a la catedral más bonita del lugar. Pero la pandemia, con su nomadismo digital y las nuevas formas de entrelazar vida personal y laboral, aceleró la necesidad de plantearse viajes diferentes.
En el año de explosión de los viajes lentos, según dicen los expertos del sector como Guillermo José Barreto, que trabaja la materia turística desde hace 23 años, analizamos con distintos viajeros contemporáneos (que nos ceden algunas de sus fotografías preferidas de sus viajes predilectos) cómo desconectar de las prisas y reconectar con el entorno -sea el que sea- de una forma más consciente. Empezando, por ejemplo, por no volar.
Es el caso de Sandra Olías, una experta en contabilidad y marketing de Barcelona que, en 2018, crea la web Viajar sin volar, donde comienza a documentar sus viajes. «Tenía fobia a volar y cada viaje en avión me hacía sentir mal. No lo disfrutaba», cuenta casi una década más tarde. «No fue una decisión premeditada ni una postura ideológica sino una manera de seguir viajando sin tener que enfrentarme a algo que me generaba malestar».
Descubrió que «viajar por tierra» le devolvía algo que ni siquiera sabía que había perdido: «La calma, el control, la sensación de que el viaje empieza justo cuando sales de casa y te subes al primer tren». Después, pensó que su experiencia, «todo lo que estaba aprendiendo», podía servirle a alguien más y empezó a narrarlo en la web, hasta convertirse en un sitio de referencia para aquellos que, por distintas razones (ambientales, personales, éticas) no quieren usar el avión.
«En mi caso no hay una sola razón», apunta Olías. «Empecé por mi cuestión personal pero ahora lo hago también por una cuestión ambiental. Cuando comparas el impacto de un vuelo con el de un tren, la diferencia es enorme», señala. Y lo explica: «Por ejemplo, un Barcelona-París en avión puede emitir más de 120 kilogramos de CO por pasajero. En tren, alrededor de 11. La reducción supera el 90%. Y esto no es una excepción: a nivel europeo, el avión emite de media cinco veces más que el tren, y en trayectos cortos puede llegar a emitir hasta 38 veces más».
Olías está hablando de lo que se conoce como flygskam, que en sueco significa «vergüenza de volar», y surge como parte del activismo ambiental en el verano de 2017: el cantante sueco Staffan Lindberg publicó un artículo junto a otras personas populares del país comprometiéndose a renunciar al avión. Entre los firmantes estaba Björn Ferry, un esquiador olímpico con medalla de oro incluida que trabajaba como comentarista deportivo. Empezó a viajar miles de kilómetros en tren para cubrir las competiciones de invierno por toda Europa y viralizó el término flygskam. Luego, se sumó la activista Greta Thunberg, que viajaba en velero, y la tendencia terminó de explotar.
En España, el pionero es Román Morales García, un aventurero nacido en Tenerife en 1962 que ha documentado sus viajes lentos, al margen de la aviación comercial, en libros como Buscando el sur (Ediciones La Palma). Lo asombroso de Morales es que viaja a pie y, a veces, hasta remando. También es «muy de andar» el escritor y viajero Gabi Martínez, quizá el mayor exponente en nuestro país de lo que se conoce como liternatura: narraciones, poemas y ensayos en los que la protagonista es la naturaleza.
«Es algo tan elemental, nuestros pies...», reflexiona Martínez en una entrevista telefónica en la que cuenta sus comienzos como viajero: «Empecé con el Interrail, durmiendo en los pasillos de los trenes, pero viajar por todo el mundo y en distintas circunstancias ha conseguido traerme a mi país, a mi familia incluso. Acabé un año en la Siberia extremeña y otro en la isla de Buda, en el delta del Ebro [escribió Delta, (Seix Barral, 2023)]. Ir con pulserita no se puede asociar a la calma, si acaso a mayor control, y un viaje debe ser todo lo contrario», señala.
Martínez habla de viajar como una «sensación» que comienza por «buscar aquel destino en el que uno se sienta más integrado con el entorno como sea posible y pensar en lo que es de verdad, como el espacio natural, donde siempre eres bienvenido y que siempre sirve de aprendizaje».
Lo que no está tan claro es que todo pichichi quiera que sus vacaciones se basen en aprender. Pero lo que no se puede negar es que desde aquella cacerolada que provocó Petrini, muchos otros pensadores han insistido en que llegaba el momento de echar el freno, en la vida en general y, en concreto, también en los viajes, que son quizá el último reducto del ser humano para desplegar sus peores instintos. Seguro que ha oído la frase: «Bueno, como aquí no me conoce nadie...».
Carl Honoré, canadiense afincado en Londres, recogió el testigo de Petrini con un libro, Elogio de la lentitud (RBA), que en 2024 cumplió dos décadas. En él, definía el Slow Travel como una forma de viajar basada en la calidad y no en la cantidad. No viajar a 40 sitios en un año sino detenerse en los lugares, adentrarse en lo local. Para Honoré, esto es un «antídoto contra la hiperaceleración»: «Frenar la marcha es un superpoder que mejora la creatividad, reduce la ansiedad y nos permite vivir con más sentido».
"Viajar lento tiene que ver con la forma en que te relacionas con un lugar. No significa necesariamente moverte despacio, sino darte tiempo para observar"
Sus palabras resuenan con las de Andrea Bergareche, una mujer que comenzó a narrar sus aventuras en internet y ahora tiene una agencia de viajes especializada en mujeres que viajan solas (Nimbala, aventuras y viajes para mujeres). Por correo electrónico, relata su punto de vista: «Para mí viajar lento tiene que ver con la forma en que te relacionas con un lugar. No significa necesariamente moverte despacio o recorrer pocos kilómetros sino darte tiempo para observar, comprender y participar de la vida cotidiana del destino. Me gusta sentarme en una terraza a observar cómo se relaciona la gente, cuáles son sus costumbres o sus pequeños rituales diarios. Me gusta hablar con locales, perderme sin un rumbo concreto por los barrios o hacer algo tan sencillo como ir al supermercado y curiosear qué productos consume la gente. Creo que muchas veces viajamos mirando los lugares, pero sin llegar a habitarlos realmente. El viaje lento consiste precisamente en eso: en dejar de ser una espectadora para convertirte, aunque solo sea unos días, en una pequeña parte de ese lugar. Cuanto más tiempo pasas observando, más empiezas a entender sus códigos, sus matices y todo aquello que normalmente pasa desapercibido cuando viajamos con prisa».
Bergareche comenzó su andadura viajera online en 2015 y dice que, «durante la última década, la transformación ha sido enorme».
«Viajar se ha vuelto más accesible y más popular que nunca, pero también se ha convertido en muchos casos en un producto de consumo rápido. Las redes sociales han tenido mucho que ver en ello. Antes llegábamos a muchos lugares con menos información y más capacidad de sorpresa. Hoy a menudo viajamos con una lista de sitios que visitar, fotos que reproducir y experiencias que consumir. Vamos al destino con una expectativa muy concreta de lo que debería ocurrir, y eso deja poco espacio para que el propio lugar nos sorprenda».
Tiene la sensación de que, mayoritariamente, «el viaje consiste en coleccionar países, monumentos, restaurantes o experiencias, a menudo sin detenernos demasiado en lo que tenemos delante». Por eso, en los viajes que organiza para mujeres, «prima el asombro y el no saber qué va a pasar». En su caso, su mejor viaje fue el que hizo en autostop por Sudamérica. «Siete meses viajando sola, durmiendo gracias a Couchsurfing con un presupuesto de solo 6-8€ diarios. Lo más valioso de aquel viaje fue precisamente no tener un plan cerrado. Eso me permitía quedarme más tiempo en los lugares que me gustaban, convivir con familias locales, participar en su día a día y dejar que fueran las personas quienes me enseñaran su realidad desde dentro. Recuerdo pasar días enteros compartiendo trayectos, comidas, conversaciones y tareas cotidianas con gente que acababa de conocer. Más que visitar lugares, sentía que estaba entrando en pequeñas vidas, en sus historias, durante unos días».
Experiencias que no aparecen en guías de viaje y que suceden porque alguien decide «dejarse llevar, estar abierto, aceptar las invitaciones, las recomendaciones y las oportunidades que van apareciendo en el camino». «Ese viaje me enseñó que muchas veces lo mejor de viajar no es lo que planeas, sino precisamente aquello que nunca habrías podido planificar y que aparece cuando dejas abierta la puerta a la posibilidad».

title: July inflation brings relief, but pressure points still expected
content:
Inflation is still higher than Sarb's target of 3%, which can result in the MPC hiking the repo rate in September.
South Africans have been given some much-needed breathing room, with inflation cooling sharply in July after hitting a two-year high the month before.
But while the latest reading offers relief for households and businesses grappling with rising costs, the respite could prove short-lived, with fuel prices, utility costs and other persistent pressures still threatening the inflation outlook.
Statistics SA (Stats SA) said annual consumer price inflation was 4.3% in July 2026, down from 5.0% in June 2026. Consumer Price Index (CPI) was released on Wednesday, revealing an increase of 0.2% month-on-month.
Inflation cools in July
Tertia Jacobs, Treasury Economist and Fixed Income Specialist at Investec, told The Citizen that the headline inflation rate came in lower than expected in July, easing to 4.3% year-on-year from 5.0% in June.
She has attributed the decline to more contained food prices, smaller increases in administered prices such as electricity and water, and a sharp slowdown in fuel inflation.
According to Stats SA, food inflation declined to just 0.6%, while fuel inflation eased to 20.6% from 34.4% in June, following reductions in petrol and diesel prices during the month.
Will inflation increase in August?
Jacobs added that other measures also suggest inflationary pressures remain relatively contained, with trimmed-mean inflation easing to 3.1% and inflation excluding fuel moderating to 3.7%.
While she welcomed the July stats, she also added that it’s important to remain “cautious about reading this as the start of a sustained decline in inflation”.
“With oil currently trading at around $91 a barrel, petrol and diesel prices are likely to rise by around R1.00 and R3.00 a litre respectively in September, putting headline inflation on course to average around 4.7% in the fourth quarter – below previous estimate of 4.9%.”
Future remains uncertain
Jacobs said the future remains uncertain as there is still no clear prospect of the Strait of Hormuz reopening, and oil-price forecasts have been revised higher for longer.
Now to the South African Reserve Bank (Sarb) – inflation is still higher than the central bank’s target of 3%, and a little over the one percentage point tolerance band.
Jacobs said it may need to reassess its oil price assumptions, which project Brent crude to average $82/bbl in 2026, and revise its July inflation projections upwards.
“Nevertheless, the Sarb’s adverse scenario – based on oil at $100 per barrel and inflation remaining above 5% for an extended period – does not currently represent our baseline, especially following July’s downside surprise (which would have been the case if the outcome had been in line with our forecast).
“The possibility of a 25bp rate increase in September remains material, but our assessed probability has declined to 50% based on the latest information.”

title: How one woman’s skin-to-skin care saves fragile infants in Tanzania
content:
Dar es Salaam. At 5:00 am every morning, Ms Mariam Mwakabungu begins a long commute from her home in Chanika to Amana Referral Hospital, where vulnerable newborn babies rely on her care.
The daily journey requires riding a motorcycle taxi (boda boda) to the bus terminal, followed by a commuter bus (daladala) to reach the facility.
Despite the financial and logistical strain, Ms Mwakabungu says her deep passion for the job keeps her motivated.
Known fondly around the hospital as 'Mama Kangaroo,' Ms Mwakabungu provides vital care for underweight newborns using the Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) method, a skin-to-skin contact technique that maintains body temperature, particularly for infants whose biological mothers are critically ill or deceased.
For over three years, she has dedicated herself to this life-saving work.
On August 5, 2026, she was seen in the neonatal ward attentively cradling an infant to ensure it received the required warmth.
"Since I started providing this service, I have felt immense peace because it is work I love from the bottom of my heart," Ms Mwakabungu told The Citizen’s sister newspaper Mwananchi.
Her responsibilities extend beyond skin-to-skin contact.
Under professional medical guidance, she feeds the infants, bathes them, and assists mothers in learning proper skin-to-skin techniques.
She also educates parents on neonatal hygiene and trains them to spot dangerous health warning signs in newborns.
Having cared for more than six infants so far, Ms Mwakabungu shared that while most go on to thrive, emotional hardships remain.
She recalled a baby named Pepetua who passed away while in her care, a loss that still pains her.
Conversely, seeing former infants growing up healthily, including one she recently reconnected with at Msimbazi Orphanage, brings her immense joy.
Senior Nursing Officer and Amana Neonatal Ward In-Charge, Ms Mary Machemba, praised Ms Mwakabungu's transition from a volunteer to a full-time employee.
The ward admits newborns aged up to 28 days, many of whom are low birth weight, orphaned, or awaiting specialised transfer to Muhimbili National Hospital (MNH).
Recognising her commitment, the hospital administration formally employed Ms Mwakabungu and facilitated on-the-job training.
She has been trained to help mothers express breast milk, calculate precise feeding volumes, bathe delicate newborns, and identify critical symptoms.
"If she notices an infant facing distress, she immediately identifies the warning signs and alerts the attending doctors or nurses," noted Ms Machemba.
"However, because she lacks formal professional qualifications and certifications, she cannot administer medications or injections. That is why we actively encourage her to pursue formal medical studies," she added.
Ms Mwakabungu had initially planned to return to school after her second child reached two years of age, but the plan was deferred when she became pregnant with her third child.
With her youngest now approaching two, she is re-evaluating options to enrol in evening classes, though balancing work at Amana, night studies, and her long commute to Chanika remains a challenge.
Her personal living conditions improved significantly two years ago when the Doris Mollel Foundation, alongside an anonymous donor, gifted her a house in Chanika, allowing her to move out of a crowded rented apartment.
The property provides ample space for her three children, room for family, and a small farming plot where she cultivates cassava and sweet potatoes.
She also hopes to construct small commercial stalls on the plot to run a retail shop selling domestic goods.
However, the relocation increased her daily travel costs, with round-trip transport expenses reaching up to Sh10,000 per day.
To manage costs, she often walks long distances to the bus station, striving to balance her professional calling at Amana Hospital with her maternal responsibilities at home.

title: Students set up little blue penguin nesting boxes along Wellington coast
content:
Intermediate students build homes for Kororā penguins
Schoolchildren are setting up nesting boxes for little blue penguins along Wellington's South Coast.
Year 7 and 8 students from Ridgway School gathered at Ōwhiro Bay this morning to install houses for kororā.
Pupils Xander, Elio and Asher said they were "really excited" about penguins using the shelter they had made.
"I'd like to see the chicks," said Elio
"I had lots of fun making these and I was pretty proud with the final product and now I'm kind of happy to see that penguins can explore and maybe enjoy it," said Xander.
They told RNZ they picked a spot for their box that was far enough away from other boxes, as penguins can be territorial.
"Because if a penguin finds a penguin house, they're going to want to have their own eggs, so they don't want any other penguins nearby," said Asher.
The boys said the project taught them about penguins' natural habitats and the threats they faced.
"Climate change, like more pets coming in, like dogs and cats. Also like the loss of bushes and stuff, so they don't have that much like cover anymore," Elio explained.
Fellow student Natalie also said she had learned about penguins: "I learned that they are very smelly."
She said she had been pretty excited about today - until she had to lift the heavy nesting box.
She said she picked her spot because it was closest to where the boxes had been unloaded from the truck.
Ridgway School teacher Nathan Crocker said the project taught the children about caring for the environment in their own backyard.
"It's just been a joy to work with the kids on this project."
As well as gaining practical skills such as woodworking, he said the students were also building character.
"Because my job in education is to create cool humans, good humans that contribute positively to society and to the environment."
Crocker said the hands-on experience would stay with them.
"You don't remember the reading, writing, and the maths. You remember the projects and the days where you did something special."
He said the project had been a collaboration with conservation charity Places for Penguins and education programme Enviroschools.
Joshua Forrest, a volunteer at Places for Penguins, said the project helped make conservation accessible and enjoyable to the next generation.
"When our bodies are slowly giving up, these guys will be out here doing all the mahi. This is the reason we're out here doing this."
He said days like today were a "highlight in the calendar".
Forrest said he admired the kororā for their resilience.
"They're such a feisty, little species. They're pretty stubborn. They defend themselves against a great deal in terms of natural predators and everything," he explained.
Unfortunately, he said, they needed help after their habitat had been fragmented and disturbed by human activity.
"When these guys are coming and going at night, when everybody's driving around the south coast - unfortunately you're not going to spot a small 30 centimetre penguin if you're driving around here at night going a little bit too fast.
"A lot of people don't realise that we have penguins everywhere (in Wellington) and so they take their dogs to places that are really, really nice for their dogs. But unfortunately it's those additional things that just really put a lot of pressure on these guys."
Enviroschools' Chloe Bisley-Wright had just experienced having to suggest a dog owner leash their animal that morning, as it wandered free near where kororā were known to be.
She said the project let children take on work in the community.
"Tamariki do care about our wildlife for sure, and it's just giving them opportunities to put that care into practical use."

title: Banyuwangi appointed as pilot site for social empowerment programme
content:
Expert Staff at the Minister, Andy Kurniawan, said the appointment was linked to the success of Banyuwangi in piloting social protection digitalisation, a programme that has since expanded to 43 districts and cities across Indonesia.
"We cannot test this poverty alleviation model in many places at once, we have to focus on a specific location. That is why we chose Banyuwangi as a pilot model and we hope the success of the social protection programme is repeated here," Kurniawan said in a written statement received here on Saturday.
He explained the program will develop an empowerment model for beneficiary families.
By so, they no longer depend solely on social assistance, but capable to build economic capacity, own assets, gain access to business opportunities, and eventually become independent and graduate from social aid.
Related news: Ministry dispatches aid, prepares compensation for NTT quake victims
Kurniawan added the PPSE is an empowerment programme covering both social and economic aspects through individual and group approaches, carried out by strengthening capabilities, asset ownership, and access to improve the welfare of beneficiary families.
The programme targets beneficiary families who are receiving Family Hope Programme (PKH) aid, basic food assistance, and parents of students at Sekolah Rakyat.
Priority is given to the residents included in deciles one to four based on National Socioeconomic Data (DTSEN), aged 19 to 64, who have received PKH and/or basic food assistance for at least one year.
Beneficiary families that have already started small businesses will be prioritised, as the programme is directed at strengthening existing economic activity. It may also be extended to residents facing social risks that meet set criteria.

title: Frenchman, sons rescued after drifting in night sea off Thailand island
content:
Brahim Terki, 50, and his sons, aged 12 and nine, were found exhausted but wearing life jackets after rescuers resumed the search early Friday morning.
The nine-year-old was found sitting on the jet ski, while his father was holding onto its side and his 12-year-old brother was floating nearby, The Nation reported.
Rescuers brought all three aboard a speedboat and took them back to shore, where medical personnel were waiting. They were later taken to hospital for further checks.
The family was located at 10:26 a.m. on Friday, around five nautical miles from Chaweng Beach in Bo Phut subdistrict, following an extensive search involving local authorities, police, rescue teams and private jet ski operators.
The boys' mother and older sister, who had remained on the beach during the search, were present when the family was reunited.
The family rented the jet ski from an operator at Chaweng Beach in Koh Samui District at around 5 p.m. on Thursday, according to the Bangkok Post.
After the 30-minute rental period ended without the family returning, despite staff signaling with a flag, the operator alerted authorities and launched a search at around 6 p.m. However, the family could not be found.
The operator initially dispatched other jet skis to search for them before authorities and members of the Koh Samui Jet Ski Club joined the operation using speedboats and additional jet skis.
A wider search involving local authorities, police, rescue teams and maritime officials was launched at about 8:50 p.m. on Thursday but was suspended around 1 a.m. due to waves reaching 3-4 meters, Thaiger reported.
The operation resumed at first light on Friday, with teams using two speedboats and 10 jet skis to search the surrounding waters.
Terki told authorities that he had taken his sons out to sea on the jet ski when rough waves hit the craft near the end of the rental period, causing its engine to stop.
Unable to call for assistance, the family spent the night stranded at sea, with Terki and his older son remaining in the water while the younger boy held onto the disabled jet ski, the Bangkok Post reported.
Terki thanked everyone involved in the rescue operation for helping the family return safely to shore.

title: Professores da UnB não aprovam greve e decidem manter assembleia permanente
content:
Docentes da Universidade de Brasília (UnB) aprovaram o indicativo de greve enquanto aguardam novos acordos com o Ministério da Gestão e da Inovação em Serviços Públicos (MGI) sobre a Unidade de Referência de Preços (URP). A decisão foi tomada durante reunião realizada na tarde desta terça-feira (18) na sede do sindicato da categoria no Campus Darcy Ribeiro.
A categoria decidiu que a deflagração sobre a greve será submetida a uma nova assembleia da categoria. A maioria dos professores assumiu uma postura cautelosa e preferiu dar continuidade nas negociações ao invés de optar por uma greve imediata.
“Os professores entenderam que hoje não era o dia de deflagrar a greve. Vamos dar um voto de confiança ao processo de negociação estabelecido entre a Advocacia-Geral da União (AGU), o MGI e a categoria. Vamos manter a mobilização e decidir sobre a deflagração da greve apenas em uma futura assembleia a ser marcada, dependendo do andamento das negociações”, afirma Pedro Gontijo, membro da diretoria da Associação dos Docentes da Universidade de Brasília (ADUnB), em entrevista ao Brasil de Fato DF.
Na última sexta-feira (14), O MGI apresentou uma proposta para tentar avançar no trâmite em torno da URP. O texto estabelece a absorção de 60% dos acréscimos remuneratórios sobre o valor da parcela, percentual que já é aplicado atualmente e que segue o acordo firmado anteriormente com os servidores técnico-administrativos.
Outro ponto envolve os professores que ingressaram recentemente na universidade. Atualmente, docentes que ingressaram a partir de dezembro de 2025 não recebem a URP. O texto original previa novembro de 2023, mas a proposta foi alterada e o novo marco temporal passou a ser dezembro de 2025. O governo propôs ampliar esse marco temporal, inicialmente até março de 2025, quando houve a decisão de mérito do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) sobre o tema. A Adunb considerou a proposta insuficiente, e o MGI se comprometeu a analisar outra data.
A proposta também prevê que promoções e progressões concedidas até 31 de março de 2026, com efeitos financeiros em abril, não sejam utilizadas para reduzir o valor da URP. Segundo a ADUnB, valores que já foram absorvidos nestes casos deverão ser restituídos. A organização reivindica que a mesma regra seja aplicada às progressões e promoções posteriores a março, ponto que ainda não houve acordo.
Greve agora ou mais negociações?
A resposta apresentada pelo governo provocou diferentes avaliações durante a assembleia. Enquanto parte dos docentes considerou insuficientes os resultados alcançados após seis rodadas, outros professores defendem que houve avanços e que as possibilidades de negociações devem continuar sendo exploradas.
Liliane Machado, professora da Faculdade de Comunicação da UnB, fez uma avaliação crítica da proposta apresentada ao MGI e defendeu a intensificação da mobilização da categoria. “O que o MGI apresentou nessa sexta mesa foi nada, absolutamente nada. […] Tudo que a gente reivindicou, a gente não conseguiu. Então são seis mesas, é zero de obtenção de qualquer coisa”, afirmou.
Professora do Departamento de Artes Cênicas Júlia Guimarães, pertence ao grupo de docentes que nunca recebeu a URP. Segundo ela, cerca de 200 professores estão atualmente nessa situação e avaliou que a possibilidade de ampliar o grupo de docentes contemplados pela parcela deve ser considerada um avanço, ainda que a reivindicação seja pela inclusão de todos.
“A discussão é sobre quanto vai ser absorvido, mas tem grupo que nunca viu essa rubrica e sabe como é o contracheque”, acrescentou. Para ela, os resultados obtidos até agora são insuficientes, mas não desconsiderados. “Pode ser um ganho pequeno, mas não é ganho zero”, afirma.
A situação dos aposentados também apareceu durante o debate. A professora Eliene Novaes, ex-presidenta da ADUnB, afirmou que 84 docentes aposentados tiveram reduções significativas no valor recebido a título de URP após decisão do Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU). Segundo ela, parcelas que variavam entre R$ 3 mil e R$ 4 mil foram reduzidas para cerca de R$ 600.
A docente também avaliou que houveram avanços nas negociações e defendeu a continuidade das tratativas do governo. “São avanços dolorosos perto daquilo que a gente gostaria, mas são avanços”, afirmou.
Para Novaes, negociação e mobilização devem caminhar juntas enquanto houver espaço para diálogo com o governo. “A nossa tarefa aqui é continuar o processo de negociação e de mobilização até quando a gente tiver espaço junto à mesa de negociação”, disse.
Negociações se arrastam há meses
A negociação é resultado de uma mobilização iniciada ainda em setembro de 2025, quando os docentes aprovaram a participação da Adunb em uma mesa específica para discutir os desdobramentos referentes à Unidade de Referência de Preços (URP). A abertura formal das tentativas, no entanto, ocorreu apenas em junho deste ano, após meses de articulações com órgãos do governo federal e a mobilização da categoria.
O impasse se intensificou em abril, quando o MGI determinou que a UnB aplicasse absorção de parte dos reajustes salariais sobre a URP. Naquele mês, os professores realizaram duas paralisações e atos públicos contra a medida.
A URP é uma parcela que representa 26,05% da remuneração que remonta às perdas salariais provocadas pela extinção, em 1989, de um mecanismo de correção de salários pela inflação. Na UnB, após decisões judiciais favoráveis a grupo de trabalhadores, o pagamento foi estendido administrativamente aos servidores da universidade em 1991 pelo então reitor Antonio Ibañez Ruiz. Desde então, a manutenção da parcela é alvo de disputas judiciais e administrativas
A primeira rodada de negociação ocorreu em 18 de junho. Desde então, os docentes têm levado quatro reivindicações centrais à mesa: a inclusão dos professores que ainda não recebem a URP, com pagamento retroativo; a revisão dos descontos aplicados aos aposentados; a discussão sobre o percentual de absorção da parcela; e a não incidência dessa absorção sobre promoções, progressões e outros acréscimos permanentes da carreira.

title: Coreografía mantiene vivo el movimiento que defendió la gratuidad en la UNAM
content:
Jueves 20 de agosto de 2026, p. 3
La justicia social, las luchas ideológicas y el activismo juvenil son el corazón de Relato: No hay inframundo, sólo laberintos, propuesta de teatro-danza de Bárbara Alvarado que evoca el espíritu del movimiento del Consejo Estudiantil Universitario (CEU), que en 1986-1987 defendió la gratuidad de la educación en la Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México.
Cinco años después de su estreno en 2021, la obra vuelve este 20 de agosto al Teatro de la Danza Guillermina Bravo en una versión revisada, más corta, más poética y más dancística, en torno a la memoria de una generación, pero desde las preguntas del presente.
En entrevista, la coreógrafa y fundadora de la compañía Aletheia Cuerpo Escénico, Bárbara Alvarado, explicó que el punto de partida no es un archivo histórico, sino una herida íntima y personal que parte de la historia de su tío Luis Alberto Alvarado, sociólogo y uno de los organizadores del CEU junto con figuras como Imanol Ordorika y Carlos Ímaz.
“Esa generación fue capaz de dar la vida por defender que la UNAM no se volviera privada. Recibieron hasta amenazas de muerte”, cuenta la coreógrafa. “Mi tío hizo su tesis sobre cómo se organizó ese movimiento. Fue una propuesta no sólo estudiantil, sino colectiva: dieron información, abrieron el diálogo con Rectoría, se televisó, usaron sus saberes, su escucha y su fuerza para resistir lo que iba a ser una catástrofe para México”.
Diez años después de la victoria estudiantil, su tío se suicidó en 1996; ese evento la marcó para toda su vida y precisamente ese suceso la llevó a crear la pieza y plantearse preguntas sobre el amor, la muerte y el misterio, es decir, la parte luminosa y al mismo tiempo dolorosa de la vida.
“Decidí darle el tiempo y momento para mirar esta herida familiar. Quise contar su historia como un héroe silencioso de México, pero también hablar de la herida masculina”, explica Alvarado. “Fue una generación que aprendió a ser fuerte, a luchar por todos, pero no a nombrar el dolor. La fortaleza real viene de aceptar la vulnerabilidad, tu propia herida, tu flaqueza, tu miedo. Si no te reconoces, te vuelves indiferente y no eres capaz de luchar por nada ni dar la vida por nada”.
Para la coreógrafa, los jóvenes de hoy siguen gozando de una universidad autónoma y gratuita “sin tener ni idea de la historia detrás”.
“Ahora que soy maestra en la Universidad Autónoma de Querétaro me pregunto en qué hemos fallado para que los jóvenes no tengan la confianza de ser ellos mismos. Hay deseo, pero el mundo les ha enseñado que no es posible. Hay indiferencia. Si no sabes de dónde vienes, no sabes a dónde vas. Si no conoces tu linaje, tu arraigo, funcionas mecánicamente. Las chicas que salen a marchar hoy, marchan porque hubo generaciones que les abrieron el camino.”
En este restreno de la pieza vuelves las preguntas al espectador: ¿cuál es tu relato? ¿Por qué has dado la vida? ¿Has hecho algo por alguien más ?
“Somos seres íntimos, familiares, sociales, políticos, ideológicos y espirituales. La trascendencia de nuestros actos afecta todos esos rubros”, comparte Alvarado.
Sobre el subtítulo de la obra No hay inframundo, sólo laberintos, la creadora señala: “Yo crecí en escuela de monjas. Cuando me dijeron ‘Beto se suicidó’, lo primero que pensé fue: ‘se fue al infierno’, porque nos enseñan que no tenemos derecho a acabar con nuestra vida. Pero si no se nos otorga el derecho a terminar con la propia vida, no entiendo por qué hay seres humanos que acaban con la vida de otros”.
Alvarado cita el libro El gesto absoluto, acerca del activista colombiano Pablo Molano, el cual plantea que el problema no es sólo el capitalismo, sino la condición que va generando en tu cerebro, en tu alma, para pensar que no tienes salida si no cumples expectativas ajenas.
“Luis Alberto no se fue al infierno, sólo estaba encerrado en un laberinto y no hubo un hilo, una Ariadna que le diera el regreso. Se lo comió el minotauro en el centro. Es una postura de no querer enjuiciar a nadie. Nunca vamos a saber las motivaciones reales de nadie, más que las tuyas.”
En esta nueva versión de Relato participan en escena cuatro intérpretes además de Alvarado, quien expresó que la distancia de cinco años le dio un punto de vista diferente. “Necesitaba afinarla, rehacerla. El tiempo nos da perspectiva. Hice un trabajo más profundo en lo corporal, lo dramatúrgico y lo metafórico”.
Para Juan Carlos Franco, dramaturgo y codirector de la pieza, volver sobre esta historia implica también revisar de manera crítica la relación entre la comunidad universitaria, su memoria y la defensa de los principios que han definido a la máxima casa de estudios.
Relato: No hay inframundo, sólo laberintos se presenta hoy y mañana a las 20 horas; el sábado a las 19 horas y el domingo a las 18 horas en el teatro Guillermina Bravo del Centro Cultural del Bosque.

title: Top towns of the NZ economy – where is the recovery firing, and where is it not?
content: The recovery feels elusive to many, but some parts of New Zealand are booming. Shamubeel Eaqub pulls together 15 indicators for every district in the country to find out who is doing well, and why. New Zealand’s economy, viewed as a whole, remains in a funk. A hoped-for recovery at the beginning of the year got trumped by Trump when he launched a war on Iran. Higher oil prices hit incomes. Fearful households and businesses pressed pause on spending, investment and job decisions. Despite a gradual improvement in some indicators over the past year, there is still a lot of pain out there. Cost of living is squeezing household budgets and unemployment is at its highest in over a decade. That is the story of New Zealand on average. But we don’t live on the average. Some sectors and occupations are doing better or worse; the same applies to parts of the country viewed from a geographic perspective. That is the focus here. I’ve pulled together 15 indicators for regions and districts (excluding the Chathams – sorry, the data is very patchy), spanning jobs, pay, housing, people, building and business, to let the data do the talking. You can play it yourself in the explorer below. The big picture, as I see it, is a north-south divide, with mainly good news in the provinces. The weakest spots are south Waikato (mill closure), Wellington (government pullback) and Northland (closures and the curse of its relative economic isolation). The south is booming Canterbury, Otago and Southland are leading the charge. West Coast is riding a wave of growth on the back of farming and mining. Northland and Wellington are really hurting. Auckland is stalled. The same shows up in our national obsession – house prices – which are down from the Covid-era super-highs in most places, but have increased sharply in Southland over the past year. This divergence of current economic fortunes isn’t about being a lucky town, it’s very much a function of good growing conditions, record commodity prices, and a resurgence in mining activity in some places. The fastest-growing districts are big on farming. The heartland has some major swagger right now and the fastest-growing are: Hurunui, where a third of the jobs are in farming, forestry, fishing and mining; Southland District, where it is 36%; Central Otago, 31%. High prices for beef and lamb, dairy and the extra cash from Fonterra’s brand sale, and even good wool prices (which hasn’t happened for decades) are all helping. But not every farming community is benefiting. So, even here it is not a rising tide lifting all, but some farms were better prepared to benefit. Urban economies are different When I look across 25 years of economic data, it’s pretty clear that urban and rural economies don’t share the same drivers. Many, of course, are similar, but construction, retail, hospitality and manufacturing are the big drivers of urban places. Rural parts of the country are heavy on the primary sector, and sometimes on one or two big industries. That can give them insulation from the economic cycle, but they are also exposed when a major employer goes – like manufacturing plant closures in Tokoroa and Hawke’s Bay, or when commodity prices fall, or drought takes grip. Farmers are always watching the weather. Predictions for a strong El Niño could mean drier than usual conditions. It’s not a 100% predictor – but a risk nonetheless. The current economic weakness is very much an urban and North Island story. It affects around 3.6 million people, or two-thirds of Kiwis. So, the provincial good news is indeed good, but its reach is small. Watch demography Across provincial New Zealand, many of the places currently enjoying good economic conditions also face big demographic pressures. While Canterbury’s population is growing at 1.1%, Marlborough and Nelson are shrinking. Many of these strong-cycle districts have little or no natural population growth, so any growth has to be imported – either from overseas or from other parts of New Zealand. Without population growth, many of these smaller provinces cannot afford long-deferred infrastructure bills (especially water), or to even upkeep their current infrastructure. If you have a job there, life can be good I hope the flush of good news gives a nudge for people to move to some of these places. The biggest export of our provinces is young people. Yet, there are jobs in these places. I see this paradox in many places: unemployed looking for work and businesses looking for workers, but not matching because they don’t have the right skills or some other barrier. Provincial wages can seem lower at first blush, but are often better after housing costs. When we look at one boiled-down measure – average pay of one filled job in each district, and subtract housing costs (a year of rent or the cost of owning the median house) – the picture is striking. Viewed nationally, the average person’s annual pay sits at about $49,600 after rent, or about $29,500 after servicing a median house that is owned. This is only a rough illustration: the best comparison would be household income net of taxes and transfers – but that is quite tricky at a district level. The top of the after-ownership list is surprising: Kawerau, Buller and Ruapehu, at roughly $43,000 to $46,000 a year left over. Cheap houses can beat high pay. Real pay is growing fastest in Clutha, Gore and Mackenzie District. In Ruapehu, Buller, Kawerau and Clutha owning is cheap relative to renting – the opposite of what we see in the big cities. At the other end of the scale is Queenstown-Lakes, which is growing insanely fast and is insanely unaffordable for the average worker. Servicing the median house there costs about $30,000 a year more than the average local job pays. The workers aren’t the owners there – it’s a two-speed economy where homes are for the very well off and hostile to the very workers who make the place function. Wellington is the mirror image The capital can boast the highest after-rent incomes in the country – about $68,800 for one job in Wellington City. It is also the region that experienced the biggest fall in business locations over the past year, while real pay fell and job ads are stuck at two-thirds of their 2019 level. This is an expensive place doing badly, and still paying well. If the provinces are having a good cycle from a hard structural position, Wellington is having a bad cycle from a strong one. One number to rule them all This is a large load of data. It can be hard to make sense of it all. So I created a composite measure to look at the cyclical position, the structural position, and the average of the two.* By District, Selwyn comes out top, then Queenstown-Lakes, Southland District, Mackenzie and Hurunui – the heartland is leading the pack. At the bottom: Buller, South Waikato, Far North and Whakatāne. By region, Canterbury and Otago lead; Nelson and Marlborough sit last. It’s just the data speaking on these measures; there will be other things happening in these places. I am just adding this caveat because I don’t want anywhere to run me out of town like they did in Whanganui. (I deserved it, after calling the river city a zombie town in 2014, after which – I assume to spite me – it started to grow strongly after decades of stagnation.) Adding back a bit of complexity But that one number flattens these different dimensions. The cyclical and structural positions both matter. One tells us how things are right now, and the other what we should be planning for. Broadly there are four camps. Eighteen districts are strong on both counts (cyclical and structural), including Selwyn, Hurunui, Mackenzie, Southland District and Queenstown-Lakes. Twelve are riding the cycle from a weak structural base, including Kaipara, Waitaki, Gore, Kawerau, Ruapehu and Dunedin. Fourteen are structurally strong but cyclically soft: Wellington City, Auckland, the Hutt cities, Porirua, Palmerston North, and Clutha. Twenty-two districts are weak on both, including the Far North, Gisborne, Rotorua and Whangārei — and, more surprisingly to me, Tauranga, Napier and Nelson. Regional data in New Zealand is of mixed quality. Sometimes I have used benefit data, which is affected by policy decisions, not just what’s happening in the economy. So, use this analysis as a way to think about places, with caveats on data quality. The signal is pretty strong. There is an economic recovery and it’s mainly rural and mainly in the south. Good growing conditions and good prices are both helping. Cheap housing means many of these places are more affordable and good places to live. Many of those places hope their current good fortunes and affordable houses will encourage people to move there – they need those people to manage the twin pressures of an ageing population and looming infrastructure renewals. More Reading * For each place I took the 15 indicators and split them into two groups: how things are moving right now (jobs growth, unemployment change, house sales, migration, real pay growth, business openings) and where the place stands structurally (unemployment level, income after housing costs, births vs deaths, building rates). Each indicator is converted to a standard score — how far above or below the average district that place sits. Extreme outliers are capped so one freak number can’t dominate, and the scores are averaged with equal weight. The cyclical and structural averages give the two sub-scores; the overall number is just the mean of the two. Zero means an average district; it’s a summary of where the data sits today, not a forecast. It’s the OECD’s standard method for building composite indicators, and the rankings barely move if you drop any single indicator. Shamubeel Eaqub is chief economist for Simplicity. title: Pramono says Jakarta economy resilient with 5.52 percent growth in Q2
content:
Jakarta’s development is aimed at driving economic growth, expanding employment opportunities, reducing inequality..Jakarta (ANTARA) - Jakarta Governor Pramono Anung said on Monday the capital’s economy remained resilient, growing 5.52 percent in the second quarter of 2026 and contributing 16.32 percent to Indonesia’s gross domestic product (GDP).
He made the remarks during a ceremony marking the 81st anniversary of Indonesia’s independence at Jakarta City Hall in Central Jakarta, on Monday.
Jakarta also kept inflation under control at 2.5 percent, which Pramono said would help support the city’s target of becoming one of the world’s top 50 global cities by 2030.
Pramono stressed that economic growth must be accompanied by a more equal distribution of the benefits of development.
“Jakarta’s development is aimed at driving economic growth, expanding employment opportunities, reducing inequality and ensuring that no resident is left behind,” he said.
In human development, the Jakarta provincial government has continued to expand access to education and improve welfare through the Jakarta Smart Card (KJP) Plus, the Jakarta Achievement Scholarship Card (KJMU), a program to waive fees for the issuance of diplomas, labor-intensive programs and support for the Sekolah Rakyat, or People’s School, initiative.
The Jakarta administration has expanded access to education and welfare through the Jakarta Smart Card (KJP) Plus, the Jakarta Achievement Scholarship Card (KJMU), a program to waive fees for the issuance of diplomas, labor-intensive programs and support for the Sekolah Rakyat, or People’s School, initiative.
“Jakarta’s progress must begin with its people. Opportunities to access education and improve quality of life must be opened as widely as possible to break the cycle of disadvantage,” Pramono said.
On the environmental front, Jakarta is promoting waste sorting at source, optimizing Reduce, Reuse, Recycle (3R) waste processing facilities and strengthening preparations for the dry season.
The city is also pursuing governance reforms, including new financing mechanisms such as municipal bonds, while maintaining an unqualified opinion from Indonesia’s Audit Board (BPK) for nine consecutive years.
“For the Jakarta provincial government, independence means providing the best possible services so that residents feel protected, safe and comfortable, and have a sense of ownership of their city through the spirit of ‘Jaga Jakarta’,” Pramono said.

title: Wales pushing the pain barrier in bid to improve
content:
Wales pushing the pain barrier in bid to improve
- Published
Sweat is pouring off Alisha Joyce and Georgia Evans as they emerge exhausted from the spin bike chamber at Wales' training base.
They collapse to the floor fighting for breath as head coach Sean Lynn gives them an encouraging tap on the back.
Next door in the gym Maisie Davies changes the playlist to "It's my birthday" while the forwards go about completing their sets in search of personal bests.
And out on the artificial pitch, Ashley Beck is putting the backs through their paces, with uncapped Amy Williams catching the eye.
This is just a glimpse of life in Wales' camp and for the players three weeks of pre-season pain is almost over.
But for Lynn and the other coaches the hard work continues as they must whittle down the squad for next month's WXV Global Series.
- Neumann back in Wales' extended WXV training squad - Published10 August

- New-look Wales end losing streak with Barbarians win - Published27 June

The want and need to be better
Wales kick-off their campaign against South Africa at Cardiff Arms Park on 18 September before hosting USA on 26 September. They will then head out to Japan for two further Tests on 23 and 31 October.
All three opponents are ranked above 12th-placed Wales, who have lost their last nine competitive fixtures.
And despite a welcome victory over Barbarians in June, Lynn's side know they are still lacking in a number of areas, notably fitness.
It is a key focus for strength and conditioning coach Gareth Harris who is out on the main pitch encouraging the players through an intense set of interval runs.
Keira Bevan is rigged with a social media microphone as she races her opposite number to a marked cone.
"We need to work harder," Harris said.
"We know where we are from a physical perspective and it is about moving that dial forward. A lot of the girls are pretty sore, but that's okay, it's all in the plan."
The 46-strong extended squad has been in camp since 3 August and trained through soaring temperatures, but Harris - who linked up with Wales before last summer's Rugby World Cup - says the attitude has been "exceptional".
"You really see the girls going 'this is important for us'," Harris said.
"We want to be better. We want to be the best team we can be. We don't just want to turn up to the international stage, we want to dominate games.
"There's ownership of the work that they're doing and ownership of our standards and how we elevate those standards and accountability to each person.
"Everybody is going 'this is what I expect of you', which is perfect for us.
"I think we'll see a different Wales this time round."
Building cohesion
Harris' optimism is echoed by forwards coach Steve Salvin who has come up to the vantage point of the barn balcony.
He clearly feels at home here having joined Lynn's backroom staff on a permanent basis with Ashley Beck in the summer.
"The four of us [coaches] were thrown together a little bit for the Six Nations, firefighting would be the wrong way to put it but obviously we were working in silos to get things sorted. Now we can be much more cohesive and collective around the way we go about doing things," Salvin said.
"We feel like there's growth in our set piece, our attack, our defence, we're essentially trying to cover all bases.
"During the Six Nations we performed reasonably well for probably 50 to 60 minutes, so one of the things we really need to go after for this series of games is performing for 80 minutes.
"If we do that, we'll give ourselves a much better chance of coming out the right side of the results."
Wales have only tasted success twice since Lynn took over in March 2025, the aforementioned Barbarians game and the first Test against Australia last summer.
But the autumn series will be seen as a major opportunity to get some wins on the board and climb back up the world rankings, where Wales were as high as sixth just three years ago.
And with the new-look WXV feeding into 2029 Rugby World Cup qualification - and a first ever Women's British and Irish Lions tour of New Zealand next September - there is plenty at stake for this group of pre-season players.

title: For students, consistent exercise may matter more for mental health than intense workouts
content: Infrequent exercise is associated with a higher prevalence of common mental disorders such as depression and anxiety among higher education students in Norway, according to a study published in PLOS ONE by Michael Grasdalsmoen of Western Norway University of Applied Sciences and colleagues. The findings highlight the potential value of consistent physical activity rather than intense, prolonged exercise sessions.

title: Jiwe la kilo 3.1 laondolewa kwenye kibofu cha mwanaume
content:
Jiwe la kilo 3.1 laondolewa kwenye kibofu cha mwanaume
- Author, BBC Sinhala
- Author, Koh Ewe

- Iliyochapishwa
- Muda wa kusoma: Dakika 5
Madaktari nchini Sri Lanka wamefanikiwa kuondoa jiwe kwenye kibofu cha mwanaume lenye uzito wa kilo 3.1 ambalo wanaamini kuwa ndilo kubwa zaidi la aina yake kuwahi kurekodiwa.
Upasuaji huo ulifanyika katika hospitali moja mjini Trincomalee, mashariki mwa nchi hiyo.
Mgonjwa huyo mwenye umri wa miaka 55 alikuwa amelazwa hospitalini baada ya kupata kiharusi. Hata hivyo, wakati akipatiwa matibabu, madaktari waligundua jiwe katika kibofu chake cha mkojo baada ya kubaini kwamba alikuwa akipata shida ya kukojoa.
Wakati wa upasuaji, madaktari waliondoa jiwe hilo la kibofu ambalo lilikuwa na uzito sawa na ule wa mtoto mchanga aliyekamilika kukua tumboni na ukubwa wake ulikuwa karibu na ule wa yai la mbuni.
"Kulingana na rekodi zilizopo, hili ndilo jiwe kubwa zaidi kuwahi kurekodiwa na kutolewa kwenye kibofu cha mkojo kupitia upasuaji," Dkt. Pragalathan Balakrishnan, aliyeongoza upasuaji huo, aliambia BBC Sinhala.
Aliongeza kuwa mgonjwa huyo ana "afya njema sana".
Madaktari walisema mgonjwa huyo bado yuko hospitalini na anaendelea kupata matibabu kwa ajili ya matatizo mengine ya kiafya aliyonayo.
Dkt. Balakrishnan aliongeza kuwa jiwe hilo huenda lilikuwa ndani ya kibofu cha mgonjwa kwa takriban miaka mitano hadi kumi.
Pata habari za kina kutoka BBC News Swahili, moja kwa moja kupitia WhatsApp.
Bonyeza hapa kujiunga
Mwisho wa Whatsapp
Mawe ya kibofu hutokea wakati madini yaliyomo kwenye mkojo yanapoganda na kuwa vipande vigumu.
Mara nyingi hutokea wakati kibofu hakitoi mkojo wote, na kuacha mkojo uliojaa madini mengi (uliofanya mgando) ambao unaweza kugeuka kuwa mawe madogo.
Mawe madogo ya kibofu, yenye ukubwa wa punje za mchanga, yanaweza kutoka yenyewe. Hata hivyo, mawe makubwa zaidi ya sentimita 1 mara nyingi huziba njia ya mkojo na kuhitaji matibabu. Jiwe la kibofu lenye ukubwa unaozidi sentimita 4 huchukuliwa kuwa kubwa sana.
Kulingana na rekodi za dunia za Guinness, jiwe kubwa zaidi la kibofu liliondolewa kwa mgonjwa nchini Brazil mwaka wa 2003. Lilikuwa na uzito wa kilo 1.9 (pauni 4.2) na urefu wa sentimita 17.9 (inchi 7).
Jiwe la kibofu lililoondolewa nchini Sri Lanka wiki iliyopita lilikuwa na urefu wa takriban sentimita 17.
BBC Tamil ilimuuliza Dkt. Balakrishnan Prahaladhan kuhusu jambo hili. Maswali aliyoulizwa na BBC Tamil pamoja na majibu yake yametolewa hapa chini.
1. Je, ni changamoto zipi zinazokabili utekelezaji wa taratibu hizi za upasuaji?
Hatukuweza kufanya upasuaji mara moja. Sababu ilikuwa ni uzito mkubwa wa jiwe hilo na pia mgonjwa alikuwa amepatwa na kiharusi.
Kama ilivyo kwa mishipa ya fahamu inayoelekea mikononi na miguuni, figo nazo zina mishipa ya fahamu. Kwa kuwa mshipa huo ulikuwa umeharibika, mtiririko wa damu uliathirika.
Kutokana na kiharusi na matatizo ya mzunguko wa damu, shinikizo ndani ya mfuko wa figo liliongezeka, shinikizo la damu likapanda, na mkojo haukutiririka kwenda chini bali ulianza kutiririka kuelekea juu kwenye figo.
Matokeo yake, utendaji kazi wa figo uliathirika. Upasuaji haukuweza kufanyika mara moja. Sababu ni kwamba mgonjwa lazima awe na nguvu mwilini ili kufanyiwa upasuaji. Ili kulinda figo, tulichukua hatua za kupunguza shinikizo ndani ya mfuko wa figo. Kulikuwa na tatizo katika hilo.
Kutokana na uharibifu uliosababishwa na jiwe hilo, ilikuwa vigumu kuingiza mirija kwenye mfuko wa figo. Ikiwa mirija hiyo haikuingizwa kwa usahihi, ilikuwa ikitoka yenyewe.
Kwa kuwa kila kitu, ikiwemo utendaji wa moyo na ubongo, kilikuwa katika hali ya kawaida, tulifanya upasuaji huo. Alilazwa hospitalini mwezi Julai. Tulikuwa tumepanga kufanya upasuaji huo mwezi Agosti.
2. Je, kuna jambo lolote lisilo la kawaida lilitokea wakati wa upasuaji huu?
Ndiyo. Aliwahi kufanyiwa upasuaji kama huu wa kuondoa jiwe dogo hapo awali. Upasuaji huo ulifanyika mwaka wa 1998. Ikiwa ni jiwe dogo, hatulitoi kwa njia ya kukata mwili; badala yake, tunaingiza kamera na kutumia leza kulivunja na kuliondoa. Hata hivyo, ikiwa jiwe ni kubwa zaidi ya sentimita 4, itachukua muda mrefu kuliondoa kwa leza. Kwa hiyo, tutalitoa kwa njia ya upasuaji wa kawaida (kukata).
Mwaka wa 1998, kutokana na ukosefu wa vifaa hivyo, alifanyiwa upasuaji kwa kukatwa tumbo. Hiyo ndiyo sababu ilikuwa na changamoto kidogo.
Kwa upande mwingine, hakukuwa na ugumu wowote katika utaratibu wa upasuaji wenyewe; ulikuwa kama utaratibu wa kawaida wa upasuaji.
3. Ilichukua muda gani kuondoa jiwe hilo kabisa na kukamilisha upasuaji?
"Ilichukua takriban saa moja."
4. Je, jiwe kubwa namna hiyo linajitengenezaje?
"Sababu kuu ya kutokea kwa mawe, hasa kwenye kibofu cha mkojo, ni kutotiririka vizuri kwa mkojo. Kwa wanaume, baada ya umri wa miaka 40 au 50, tezi iliyo chini ya kibofu cha mkojo huwa kubwa.
Inapokuwa kubwa mkojo hautiririki ipasavyo na inakuwa vigumu kukojoa. Mtu huhisi kukojoa mara kwa mara. Hata baada ya kukojoa, bado kuna hisia ya kutaka kukojoa tena, na mtu huhisi kulazimika kuamka usiku. Hii ndiyo sababu ya hali hiyo inayojulikana kama 'Lutz'.
Hali kama hiyo inapokuwepo, kuna uwezekano wa kupata maambukizi ya figo. Sababu hizi mbili zinaweza kusababisha kutokea kwa mawe kwenye mfuko wa figo.
Hii ndiyo sababu mawe hutokea kwenye mfuko wa figo. Vinginevyo, mawe kutoka kwenye figo yanaweza kushuka hadi kwenye kibofu na kutengeneza mawe huko. Hata hivyo, ni nadra sana mawe hayo kuwa makubwa.
Jiwe linaposhuka kutoka kwenye figo, mgonjwa huhisi maumivu. Kwa hiyo, jiwe hilo linaweza kugundulika mapema. Tatizo la kukojoa linapokuwepo, jiwe hilo litaendelea kuwa kubwa zaidi ikiwa halitashughulikiwa.
5. Unadhani ilichukua muda gani kwa jiwe hili kukua na kufikia ukubwa huu?
"Huenda ilichukua takriban miaka 5 hadi 10."
6. Kuna taarifa kwamba jiwe kubwa zaidi duniani limeondolewa kwenye kibofu cha mkojo. Je, hilo ni kweli?
"Hili ndilo jiwe kubwa zaidi kuwahi kurekodiwa. Tumewasilisha maombi ya kutambuliwa na Rekodi za Dunia za Guinness. Bado kuna hatua chache zilizosalia. Rekodi ya awali katika nyanja hii ni ya jiwe lenye uzito wa kilo 1.9 lililoondolewa nchini Brazil mwaka wa 2003."
7. Je, mgonjwa huyu aliwezaje kuhimili jiwe kubwa kiasi hicho?
Tulizungumza na wanafamilia. Jiwe hilo lilionekana waziwazi. Kulikuwa na uvimbe tumboni ambao hata mtu asiye na ujuzi wa kimatibabu angeweza kuutambua.

title: BRUCE PEARL: Conservatives are attacking the very college sports bill that protects women
content:
Men don’t belong in women’s sports. That isn’t complicated, but some conservative influencers and interest groups are allowing it to become complicated through careless claims about legislation designed to protect college athletics.
I spent nearly five decades coaching college basketball. I know the difference between winning a possession and winning the game. Conservatives now face a similar choice: We can chase applause by attacking allies and mischaracterizing the bill, or we can unite around the facts and win the larger fight for women, fairness and the future of college sports.
Some organizations and women’s-sports advocates claim the Protect College Sports Act would "gut" Title IX or invalidate state laws that reserve women’s teams for women. They are wrong. The text says the opposite.
REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: COLLEGE SPORTS BILL ENTERS LEGISLATIVE 'RED ZONE' AS SEASON KICKS OFF
Section 127 explicitly states that nothing in the bill will "override, modify, or amend" Title IX. Female athletes would retain their current legal protections and ability to bring sex-discrimination claims. Section 120 also protects athletes, employees and others from retaliation for reporting discrimination or participating in Title IX proceedings.
I spent nearly five decades coaching college basketball. I know the difference between winning a possession and winning the game. Conservatives now face a similar choice: We can chase applause by attacking allies and mischaracterizing the bill, or we can unite around the facts.
Critics also claim the bill would erase state laws keeping men out of women’s sports. It would not. The legislation establishes national standards for Division I and Division II competition on limited eligibility questions, including academics, professional status, legal violations, age and years of eligibility. It neither creates a federal right for men to enter women’s competitions nor pre-empts state laws establishing sex-based athletic categories.
The bill does not expressly create a federal right for biological males to compete in women’s sports, and Section 127 states that nothing in the bill overrides, modifies or amends Title IX. Critics seem to be grasping at anything and eager to disregard the Title IX provisions here. Especially since the Supreme Court ruled in June that schools may keep men out of women’s sports.
It also requires governing bodies to enforce rules related to state and federal law and allows individuals to sue when the law is violated.
CONGRESS MUST FIX THE PROTECT COLLEGE SPORTS ACT BEFORE GIRLS PAY THE PRICE
The bill also gives schools a powerful incentive to invest in women’s and Olympic sports. It creates a $22.5 million athlete-retention fund and allows schools to unlock up to an additional $5 million through eligible NIL investments in women’s, Olympic and non-revenue sports. A school seeking the full $27.5 million retention allowance would first need to invest $5 million in those sports. That is an ingenious way to ensure continued investment in programs that might otherwise be left behind.
And every year Congress waits, the financial pressure on college athletics grows, and the programs with the fewest resources become even more vulnerable. My 2025 Final Four team had a total NIL budget of approximately $4 million. By the 2027 Final Four, some teams could be operating with budgets approaching $30 million.
Conservatives should debate legislation, demand improvements and scrutinize every line. But facts must guide us. Too many Washington organizations would rather score points against perceived rivals than secure lasting victories for women and college athletes.
Outrage is easy; turning shared principles into law is harder. Infighting only helps the left, which has spent years undermining Title IX while conservatives battle over legislation that expressly preserves it. If we can’t unite and get this done, we will lose college sports as we know them, and women’s and Olympic sports will continue to be among the first casualties.
The stakes extend beyond Title IX, and the crisis is no longer theoretical. Thirty-two Division I Olympic-sports programs were cut between the announcement of the House settlement and May 2025. WRAL reported that more than 40 Division I Olympic-sports programs were cut between May 2024 and July 2025, even though 75% of American Olympians in 2024 competed in collegiate athletics. NCAA data
Even the University of Arkansas, backed by SEC resources, announced plans to eliminate its tennis programs before donors intervened to save them. If programs at schools like Arkansas are vulnerable, imagine the danger facing smaller schools, women’s teams and non-revenue sports nationwide.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION
Credit where credit is due: Sens. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, and Eric Schmitt, R-Mo., and others have stepped up to move this legislation forward. President Trump has also led from the front by restoring the biological meaning of sex in federal policy, taking action to save college sports and backing this bill. Now, those who claim to support the America First movement should get in the game, help Congress finish the job and deliver this win for women and college athletes.
Congress now has the opportunity to take important steps to stabilize college sports, support educational opportunities for young women and men, and provide protections for the uniquely American experience of intercollegiate athletics.

There is broad agreement that college sports cannot go on with no meaningful guardrails around eligibility, transfer policy and NIL oversight. The Protect College Sports Act is an important step in the right direction, and Congress needs to keep the positive momentum moving forward.
Winning the point may feel good. Winning the war matters more.

title: Lung cancer patient becomes tumor-free after treatment with selenite
content: A patient with advanced, treatment-resistant lung cancer became tumor-free after treatment with the selenium compound selenite. This is shown in a new study from Karolinska University Hospital and Karolinska Institutet published in the journal Oncology and Therapy as a case report. The findings may contribute to increased knowledge about selenite as a possible cancer treatment.

title: Buscar nuevo hogar para un perro o un gato: qué dice un estudio sobre esta decisión
content:
Buscar un nuevo hogar para un perro o un gato: qué dice un estudio sobre esta difícil decisión
Basado en hechos observados y verificados directamente por nuestros periodistas o por fuentes informadas.
Elígenos como tu fuente preferida en Google.
Una investigación identifica tres grandes perfiles de familias que reubican a sus animales y evidencia el fuerte estigma que todavía existe.
Cuando una persona publica un mensaje buscando un nuevo hogar para su perro, su gato, o cualquier animal mascota, las reacciones en redes sociales suelen ser inmediatas y no es raro encontrar insultos, amenazas y acusaciones de abandono, antes incluso de conocer las circunstancias que han llevado a esa familia a tomar una decisión tan difícil.
Sin embargo, la realidad suele ser mucho más compleja. Existen enfermedades, problemas de vivienda, cambios laborales incompatibles, separaciones traumáticas, dificultades económicas sobrevenidas y situaciones familiares inesperadas que pueden hacer imposible seguir ofreciendo al animal la calidad de vida que merece. En esos casos, encontrarle otro hogar estable puede convertirse precisamente en una forma de proteger su bienestar y de demostrar que nos importa.
Una investigación reciente ha analizado por primera vez los distintos caminos que siguen las personas que deben reubicar a un animal de familia. Sus conclusiones muestran que detrás de estas decisiones existen circunstancias muy diferentes y que, lejos de tratarse de actos impulsivos, muchas personas intentan durante meses encontrar alternativas antes de dar el paso definitivo.
Reubicar no es abandonar
Lo primero que conviene aclarar es que buscar un nuevo hogar de manera responsable no equivale a abandonar un animal. El abandono implica dejar al perro o al gato sin cuidados, sin supervisión o en un lugar del que no pueda regresar, poniendo en riesgo su vida y su bienestar.
La reubicación responsable, por el contrario, consiste en transferir su cuidado a otra persona, familia o entidad que pueda seguir proporcionándole una vida adecuada cuando la convivencia resulta objetivamente inviable. Eso no significa que todas las reubicaciones sean acertadas ni que cualquier motivo las justifique, pero tampoco que todas respondan a una irresponsabilidad o por una falta de compromiso. De hecho, el estudio pone de manifiesto que las circunstancias son muy diversas y que generalizar conduce a conclusiones injustas.
Tres situaciones detrás de una misma decisión
Los investigadores encuestaron a 452 personas de Estados Unidos y Canadá que habían reubicado a un animal durante los cinco años anteriores. Tras analizar conjuntamente todos los factores implicados, identificaron tres grandes perfiles, muy diferentes entre sí.
El grupo más numeroso, que representó el 47,6% de los participantes, estaba formado por personas que atravesaban dificultades personales o relacionadas con la vivienda. Pérdida del hogar, cambios familiares y problemas de salud hacían imposible continuar cuidando del animal en condiciones adecuadas.
El segundo grupo, correspondiente al 42,9%, estaba compuesto principalmente por personas que habían incorporado recientemente al animal y descubrieron que la convivencia no era viable. En muchos casos convivían ya con otros animales, surgieron problemas económicos o comprobaron que la integración era mucho más complicada de lo esperado.
El tercer grupo, menos frecuente con un 9,5%, reunía a quienes tuvieron que tomar la decisión por problemas graves de comportamiento, especialmente cuando existían conflictos con otros animales y riesgos para los menores de la familia. Lejos de responder a un único patrón, el estudio demuestra que las causas suelen combinarse y empeorar con el tiempo.
La mayoría de personas intenta encontrar soluciones
Uno de los datos más interesantes es que muchas familias no toman la decisión de inmediato ni de actúan de forma irreflexiva. Entre quienes habían incorporado recientemente al animal, el 55% había buscado algún tipo de ayuda para intentar mantener la convivencia. En el grupo que atravesaba dificultades personales y de vivienda también buscó ayuda el 46%.
Las alternativas fueron muy variadas. Algunas personas recurrieron a familiares y amigos para cuidar temporalmente del animal, otras contrataron estancias en residencias caninas, modificaron sus horarios laborales y buscaron asesoramiento profesional sobre comportamiento. Sin embargo, muchas de esas soluciones terminaron siendo insuficientes.
Algunos participantes explicaban que los amigos que les ayudaban dejaron de poder hacerlo, mientras que otros reconocían que los servicios de residencia canina acababan siendo económicamente inasumibles a lo largo del tiempo.
Todas estas experiencias ponen de manifiesto que la decisión rara vez se limita a un momento concreto, sino que suele ser el resultado de un proceso largo y emocionalmente agotador.
El peso del juicio social
Los investigadores comprobaron que muchas personas manifestaban una importante preocupación por cómo serían juzgadas por los demás. Paradójicamente, quienes más temían esas críticas eran precisamente quienes habían incorporado recientemente al animal y acababan descubriendo que la convivencia no era posible.
Esta presión social, seamos claros, no ayuda a mejorar el bienestar animal. En algunos casos incluso puede retrasar las decisiones necesarias ante la fuerte coacción social, prolongando situaciones de estrés tanto para el animal como para la propia familia.
Es importante recordar que nadie conoce las circunstancias personales que existen detrás de una publicación en redes sociales. Enfermedades, violencia de género, pérdida de empleo, desahucios, diagnóstico de discapacidad, fallecimientos o cambios familiares pueden alterar completamente la capacidad para seguir cuidando de un animal, incluso cuando existe un fuerte vínculo afectivo.
Convertir automáticamente a esas personas en un objeto de ataques públicos no favorece a nadie y puede dificultar que busquen una solución responsable.
Responsabilidad y compromiso
En ocasiones, mantener a un animal en una situación claramente incompatible con nuestras necesidades puede resultar más perjudicial que encontrarle un hogar donde pueda recibir la atención adecuada. Esto puede ocurrir, por ejemplo, cuando el titular debe permanecer hospitalizado durante largos periodos, pierde definitivamente la vivienda, desarrolla una enfermedad incapacitante o atraviesa circunstancias que hacen imposible cubrir las necesidades básicas del animal.
También existen casos de incompatibilidades de convivencia que no logran resolverse pese a los intentos realizados, especialmente cuando existe un riesgo real para otros animales o para personas vulnerables.
Aceptar que una situación ha dejado de ser sostenible no implica necesariamente falta de amor. En muchos casos supone reconocer los propios límites y priorizar el bienestar del perro o del gato por encima del deseo de mantenerlo junto a uno mismo.
Más apoyo y menos estigmas
Los autores del estudio consideran que estos resultados pueden servir para diseñar ayudas mucho más específicas para las familias que atraviesan dificultades antes de llegar a la reubicación.
Entre las medidas que proponen se encuentran facilitar apoyos temporales, mejorar el acceso a recursos relacionados con el comportamiento animal, reforzar las redes comunitarias de ayuda y ofrecer soluciones adaptadas a las distintas circunstancias familiares. Comprender que no todas las historias son iguales también puede contribuir a reducir un estigma que continúa muy presente.
Aunque nos encontremos en una época donde se romantiza compartir vida con un animal, la convivencia supone asumir una enorme responsabilidad y un compromiso para toda su vida. Precisamente por eso, cuando circunstancias extraordinarias hacen imposible seguir cumpliendo ese compromiso, buscarle un hogar donde pueda seguir disfrutando de una vida segura, estable y feliz no debería convertirse automáticamente en motivo de condena pública. En muchos casos, lejos de ser un acto de abandono, puede representar una de las decisiones más dolorosas y generosas que una familia llegue a tomar.

title: [Research] Assessing Patient Compliance and Long-Term Outcomes of Oral Appliances in Sleep Apnea Management
content:
Assessing Patient Compliance and Long-Term Outcomes of Oral Appliances in Sleep Apnea Management
DOI:
https://doi.org/10.54536/ajmsi.v5i2.7890Keywords:
Long-Term Outcomes, Obstructive Sleep Apnea, Oral Appliance Therapy, Patients Satisfaction, Sleep Quality, Treatment EffectivenessAbstract
Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) was identified as a common chronic sleep disorder causing serious physiological, psychological, and functional impairments; and Oral Appliance Therapy had been developed as an effective alternative to traditional treatment due to its portability, comfort, and patient satisfaction. The objective of this study was to determine the patient compliance and long-term results (both subjective and objective) of oral appliance therapy in the management of sleep apnea by assessing comfort, ease of use, treatment effects, side effects, patient satisfaction, and their association with long term adherence. A quantitative cross-sectional research design was adopted and data were collected with a structured questionnaire from 422 diagnosed patients of sleep apnea. Sample size was calculated using Cochran’s formula and Analysis & interpretation of the collected data were done by descriptive and inferential statistics using IBM SPSS Statistics. The findings demonstrated high levels of patient adherence, comfort, perceived treatment effectiveness and long-term health improvement among the individuals surveyed. It was also discovered that patient satisfaction levels were high and had a robust acceptance, coupled with an equally strong positive behavioral intention toward continued use of Oral Appliance Usage. Moderate side effects (gastrointestinal or related to the infusion), and difficulties in adjusting behavior confronted by both patients and staff were reported but had no significant impact on continuing treatment. Results indicated that stronger compliance and perceived effectiveness predicted better long-term health states and quality of life outcomes whilst manageable side effects did not influence sustained use. Oral appliance therapy is a successful and patient-centered treatment option for sleep apnea that has proven to make an important contribution to improved clinical outcomes and long-term compliance when administered under proper direction and continuing follow-up care.
